calibration_rulings.ruling: As b1 ruled: «آباد» for a mosque in use, in card, summary and body; it names no time at which a visitor may come. Read by two readers; unchanged.
calibration_rulings.guard: None.

calibration_rulings.title: The Jabrids: «بنو جبر», or the file's own «الجبور»; and how the name stands in a phrase.
calibration_rulings.binds: jabri-mosque summary and body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «بنو جبر». Wherever the name stands on the page it is followed by the Urdu possessive and the sources' own noun, «بنو جبر کی ریاست» — in the summary («بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور کی ایک مسجد») as in the body («بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور میں») — and «بنو جبر کے دور» is not written: one reader read «جبر کے دور» in it as the set phrase for an age of tyranny, and two read the fuller phrase without a stumble. The summary so follows the Arabic summary ('from the era of the Jabrid state') and the English body, where the English summary shortens to 'Jabrid-era': a change of form under ruling P23, logged among the source's defects with the literal wording. «قبیلہ» is not written before the name (item N27: the rider on tribes does not reach a ruling house). The entry stays pending while the attestation is two pages. Final.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on the page the dynasty's name is always followed by the possessive and the word for a state, never straight by the word for an era.

calibration_rulings.title: What visitors are called on a page that is not a mosque (the question b1's item N17 left to this batch).
calibration_rulings.binds: khuzam body; every later page that is not a mosque.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. «زائرین» does not stand off a mosque page; where a noun for visitors is written on a page whose subject is not a place of worship, it is «سیاح» (oblique plural «سیاحوں»), the word the interface uses of them. A phrase that is neither noun is not touched (b1's al-uqair says 'the one who comes'). On khuzam: «اسے سیاحوں کے لیے کھول دیا گیا». C is the commonest frame for a monument and is on record for the owner; it was not taken because it changes the source's noun where a common Urdu word for it exists. Cost, stated: «سیاح» is a shade narrower than 'visitors'.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the mosque word for visitors stands on mosque pages only.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The emirate building' («مبنى الإمارة») in the list of the port's buildings on uqair-castle: the literal pair, or the Urdu name of a seat of government?
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-castle body. Any later page that names the emirate building of the port.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, final for this page. The source names whose building it is and nothing else, and the Urdu says as much: «امارت کی عمارت». B and C are one word in two spellings, and that word says a ruler's seat, his residence, a royal palace: it is not written for this building, whatever one reader made of it — the fence outranks fluency, and the site rule on the palace of Al-Uqair is the owner's. The entry round 2 added for B is withdrawn and its key retired; with it fall the questions of its spelling against the dictionary's headword and of its gender. The cost of A is the Urdu's own and is charged under nativeness and fit on uqair-castle: two look-alike words side by side, and «امارت» is also wealth. No fourth wording is made in the last round. For the judge of the next page that lists this building: the remedy, if there is one, is in the source — a word saying what the building was.
calibration_rulings.guard: The key this entry retires is read by the stage checker. For the proofreader, not machine-read: on uqair-castle the list of the port's buildings has five nouns, and none of them says a seat, a residence or a palace.

calibration_rulings.title: The order of an area line whose source names no larger place as a bare name ('Al-Battaliyah village — northeast of Hofuf', 'Al-Koot district — central Hofuf').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::area, unchanged. BINDS b4: hubaish «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں», umzurainiq «محلہ العویمریہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں» and uqair-mosque's area line keep the source's order as they stand. Round 1's six lines (al-uqair, jawatha-mosque, ameeriah, khuzam, baiah, uqair-castle) stand unchanged. Every later area line of the pattern. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source's area line names no larger place as a bare name — it gives a village, a quarter or a port and then where that lies by a direction or a part of the town — the Urdu keeps the source's order: the place with its generic, then «،», then the position, which ends in a postposition: «البطالیہ گاؤں، ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں», «محلہ الکوت، ہفوف کے وسط میں». Ruling P20 is untouched and holds wherever the source names a larger place as a bare name: that place leads («ہفوف، محلہ الکوت»; «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التہیمیہ گاؤں»). The two orders are therefore two cases of one rule — what the source gives as a bare larger name leads, and what it gives as a position follows — and no line of round 1 moves. Cost, stated: the same quarter can still stand quarter-first on one page and town-first on another where its sources word the line differently; that is logged with the sources' defects and is the owner's to even out in the source. On record for him, one line: B for every such line («ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، البطالیہ گاؤں»), which would move ten lines on applied pages. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted as b3's judge ruled it; nothing moves. hubaish::area and umzurainiq::area keep the source's order and end in a postposition; uqair-mosque::area is the approved line of uqair-castle from the translation memory, which also ends in one; tahimiyah-e and abubakr-mosque lead with the larger bare place (ruling P20). b4's first reader read the five rows and remarked, as a minor item, that the row is built four different ways and that he had to re-orient each time (observation 7): the two cases of this rule over four wordings of the sources, logged with the sources' defects as this entry says. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 on b4 are these three lines and are expected. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader of b4 (his item 47, minor) notes that abubakr-mosque's row puts the town first where hubaish and umzurainiq put the quarter first: the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings, logged as before. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 are still these three lines. ‖ b5, ROUND 1: adopted and applied on four lines. The sources of shaban, kanzan, arbaa and thulaim give two positions and name no larger place as a bare name, so each line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition: «التویثیر کے قریب، ہفوف کے مشرق میں», «ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، الشعبہ اور الکلابیہ گاؤں کے قریب», «ہفوف کے جنوب مشرق میں، الطرف نامی قصبے کے قریب», «العیون شہر کے مغرب میں، الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں». tuwaither's source names the larger place bare and its line leads with it (ruling P20): «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التویثیر گاؤں», the approved build of both tahimiyah lines. The stage checker's four notes of ruling P20 on b5 are these four lines and are expected. In round 1 arbaa's line changed only in the place of the town's generic (item N73-generic-for-a-town); what thulaim's second position says is item N74-area-line-north-of-al-ahsa. The first reader (his item 42, moderate) notes that tuwaither's row is built differently from the other four: the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings, logged as before. ROUND 2: arbaa's line changed again by one word, «نامی», between the town's name and its generic (item N73-generic-for-a-town as amended; round 2's change 6); it keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition. The other four lines are round 1's. The second reader, too, notes that tuwaither's row is built differently from the other four (his item 38): the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: its note of ruling P20 on an area line of this pattern is expected and is not a finding. For the proofreader, not machine-read: an area line that does not open with a bare larger place has a source that names none, and ends in a postposition, never in a bare place name after the comma.

calibration_rulings.title: A Hijri year or century whose Gregorian equivalent the source marks as approximate ('1280 AH (around 1863 CE)', 'the fifth century AH (around the eleventh century CE)').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body (the century), bubakr-ribat::body (two years). BINDS b4, unchanged: hubaish body «تیرہویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً انیسویں صدی عیسوی)». Every later page with such a pair. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source gives a Hijri year or century and marks its Gregorian equivalent as approximate, the form is ruling N12's (or N11's) with the one word «تقریباً» inside the round bracket, before the Gregorian figure or ordinal: «1280 ہجری (تقریباً 1863 عیسوی)», «1430 ہجری (تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)», «پانچویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً گیارہویں صدی عیسوی)». The word stands only where the source has it and only on the side the source puts it: where the source's 'around' covers the Hijri date itself it stands before the pair, as on jabri-mosque («تقریباً 850 ہجری (1446 عیسوی)»). Nothing is converted, computed or evened out between pages: 1430 AH is «(2009 عیسوی)» on jalaniyah and «(تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)» on bubakr-ribat because their sources say so. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; the bracket of hubaish is unchanged. Since b4's round 1 the pair is followed by another verb, «تیرہویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً انیسویں صدی عیسوی) میں تعمیر ہوئی» (change 3 of b4's round 1, counted from 0), the frame of jalaniyah. b4's first reader read the pair twice (observations 9 and 22) and did not stumble on its form. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader read the pair without a stumble on its form; his items 13 and 45 are on the sources' unevenness.
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read clauses of rulings N11 and N12 hold as they are (the stage checker passes this form under both). For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word for 'around' stands inside the bracket only where the source marks the Gregorian side as approximate, and is the round's one word for it.

calibration_rulings.title: Does the name «رباط آل ابی بکر الملا» owe a gloss on its own page (ruling P3c, point 1)?
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat: title, summary, body. Any later page whose name begins with «رباط»: bare, with what the place is said in the summary and at the opening of the body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. No bracket. «رباط» is an Urdu word and not an opaque generic (case a), and it is not shown to be a false friend (case b): the one reader who met it understood what the place is from the page's own words before the body began. The name stands bare in title and body; the summary, which renders first, says what the place is in the source's own words («ایک علمی وقف»), and the second sentence of the body says it again. B's bracket would say «سرائے» of a place the sources call an endowment for students, and C adds a noun neither source has. The word is masculine and the page's own text agrees with it so.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on bubakr-ribat no bracket follows the name, and the summary and the second sentence of the body say what the place is.

calibration_rulings.title: A «بیت X» name met in passing: bare, or with «نامی» and an Urdu generic (ruling P3c, point 2, lists neither)?
calibration_rulings.binds: dibs::body. Every later passing mention of «بیت البیعہ» or «بیت الملا».
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. «بیت» joins the generics of ruling P3c, point 2, that are Urdu words: a «بیت X» name met in passing stands bare, with no bracket and no «نامی». What the place is belongs to its own page, where its gloss stands by cases (c) and (d). B would call a building «گھر» that is a museum today, which the passing page's source does not say.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a name that begins with «بیت» and is not the page's title stands bare.

calibration_rulings.title: The gloss of the page's own name on qubba-mosque: an application of ruling P3c, point 1, cases (c) and (d).
calibration_rulings.binds: qubba-mosque::body; the summary and the title carry no bracket.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as ruling P3c gives it: «مسجد القبہ (یعنی گنبد والی مسجد)» once, at the first mention in the body, a noun with its describing phrase and no possessive; never in the title, the summary or a label. The summary says the same thing in plain words without the name, as its source does.
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read clause of ruling P3c as it is (the opener of the gloss once on a page, straight after the page's own title).

calibration_rulings.title: A byname the source itself quotes and the English translates ('the village of forty mosques'): marks, gloss, «نامی»?
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-05 has it: tahimiyah-e body carries the same clause word for word after its own opening words («خود یہ گاؤں»); its summary, whose English has a count and no byname, keeps «چالیس مساجد» without marks. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as a fourth place for quotation marks beside the three of ruling N16, point 5: a byname that the source itself sets in quotation marks and the English translates is written translated, inside U+201C and U+201D, with no gloss and no «نامی» (it is not a P3b name: nothing of it is Arabic). Its plural is the page's own («مساجد»). The shared clause, from its first word to its stop: «کبھی “چالیس مساجد کا گاؤں” کے نام سے مشہور تھا، اور ان مساجد میں سے اب تقریباً گیارہ ہی باقی ہیں۔» — 'only' is the particle and 'around' the round's one word, both the source's; that the two pull against each other (observation 47) is the source's sentence. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e body carries the shared clause after its own opening words, equal to b3's by script, and its summary keeps the count without marks. b4's first reader read the byname in its marks without a remark; what he noticed in the clause is the approximate word before a small count (observation 8), which is the source's. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader read the byname in its marks without a remark; his item 12 is again the approximate word before a small count, the source's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the byname stands inside its quotation marks at every mention, translated, with no bracket after it.

calibration_rulings.title: An Hours value that gives no clock time ('Open to visitors during daylight hours', Arabic 'available for visiting throughout the daylight hours').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::practical[1].value. BINDS b4, as SHARED-04 has it: tahimiyah-e practical[1].value is this string byte for byte. The label is the approved «اوقات». ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B, one string on both pages: «دن بھر زائرین کے لیے کھلی رہتی ہے». Where the two sources differ in strength the Arabic is followed ('throughout the daylight hours'), and that is counted under accuracy against the English's 'during'. No clock time is supplied, nothing is tied to prayer times, and the row is carried into no other field. That an Hours row stands on a mosque page beside the owner's fixed row, and what the owner's pending question would make of it, is logged for him; neither wording answers it. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e practical[1].value equals b3's string by script. b4's first reader (observation 19, minor): the row repeats the row above it, and the value is 'at least something to plan with, though it does not say from when to when' — the source's; no fault in the wording. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 16, moderate): the value leaves him unsure about the sunset and night prayers, and the page does not say whether prayers are held today — the source's; no fault in the wording.
calibration_rulings.guard: The two values are equal by script. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value names no hour and ends without a stop.

calibration_rulings.title: A mosque with more than one prayer niche and with arches named in the same breath: ruling N34 marks the niche by the singular, which cannot hold here.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. b4: its pages with arches (hubaish, umzurainiq) name no niche in the plural beside them and are not touched; the rule binds b4 only if such a sentence arises.
calibration_rulings.ruling: E. Round 1 ruled B and named the next blind reader as its test; B failed it and is withdrawn. On a page where niches in the plural and arches both stand, they do not share a sentence, and the arches are said first, among the materials and the roof and before any niche has been named: «ستونوں کی قطاروں پر نوک دار محرابیں ٹکی ہیں۔» Then the niches, with the wall and their number: «قبلے کی دیوار میں دو محرابیں اس مسجد کو منفرد بناتی ہیں۔» No word changes and none is added; the order of two statements of one source sentence is turned, which is form (ruling P23). D is not taken: ruling N34 keeps one word for the arch and a batch judge does not reopen it. C drops the source's noun. The cost of E is on record: one word still names two things in neighbouring sentences, and E has been read by no one; the next blind reader is its test. IF HE STUMBLES TOO, nothing inside ruling N34 is left to try: the text is then locked with E or B, whichever that round's judge finds the less harmful, and the cure both readers of this batch wrote, D, goes to whoever may reopen N34 — its mark for the arch (the plural) fails on a page whose niches are plural. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: nothing moves; neither page of b4 with arches names a niche. RECORDED for whoever may reopen ruling N34: b4's first reader (observation 24, moderate) pictured several prayer niches in a veranda at «گول محرابوں والا برآمدہ» (hubaish) before he worked out that arches are meant, and on umzurainiq cannot tell which is meant in «دیواروں، کھڑکیوں اور محرابوں پر گچ کے نقش و نگار». The plural, which is the mark ruling N34 gives the arch on a mosque page, was in place both times. He is the third reader of this round to take the plural for niches on a mosque page, and the first to do so on pages that name no niche at all: b3's round 2 records that the mark fails where the niches are plural; here it failed where there are none. A batch judge does not reopen N34, and the cost is charged under nativeness on both pages. b3's round 2 turned the order of its two sentences (candidate E); that moves nothing in b4. b4, ROUND 2: nothing moves. The second reader of b4 (item 26, minor) also took the arches of hubaish for prayer niches 'for a moment' and names umzurainiq's plural with it: the fourth reader of the round, and the second on pages that name no niche. Recorded as before for whoever may reopen ruling N34. ‖ AFTER THE LAST BLIND READ (b3/stages/06-blind-reader.on-r2.md, item 12, moderate; no judge round followed it): the reader of E stumbled too. He took the second sentence for two of the arches, read it twice, and wrote the word of candidate D for the first sentence. The final text carries E; D goes to whoever may reopen ruling N34.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on jalaniyah the sentence of the arches stands before the sentence of the two niches, and the two are two sentences.

calibration_rulings.title: The Urdu title where title_en keeps only the place name and translates the rest ('Al-Tahimiyah West Mosque').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::title. BINDS b4, as SHARED-02 has it: tahimiyah-e «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد»; uqair-mosque's title is built the same way. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, one pattern for a title whose English translates everything but the place name: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, then the translated words in Urdu order — «التہیمیہ کی مغربی مسجد», «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد». The note ruling N14 added to the title rule (the Arabic generic first) is for names whose generic the English keeps, and is not touched. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e's title and its second name on the same pattern stand, and uqair-mosque's title is ruled under b4's item N56-title-with-two-possessives. The cost, on b4's first reader (observations 12 and 14): the title reads to him as a description, 'the eastern mosque of the village', not as what the mosque is called; and with the second name of abubakr-mosque, which its source translates the same way, he wondered whether two pages were about one mosque. The names are the sources'. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 14, moderate) says both things again: on tahimiyah-e he cannot tell whether «مشرقی مسجد» is the mosque's name or 'the eastern one', and with the second name of abubakr-mosque he went back to check that they are two places. Two readers of two: the stated cost, charged under fit on tahimiyah-e.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: such a title begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it, and carries no Arabic adjective with an article.

calibration_rulings.title: The Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', or the press's loan?
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-08 has it: uqair-mosque body writes the same key in the same oblique form. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The body is «الجبیل اور ینبع کا شاہی کمیشن»: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', the loan ruling N18 admits for a body called a commission, the two cities with the Urdu possessive; no quotation marks, and it inflects like any phrase (ruling N16, point 4) — in a sentence «الجبیل اور ینبع کے شاہی کمیشن نے». The press form goes to the entry for search and is not written. The entry stays pending for one reason only: nothing in Urdu attests this wording for this body. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; uqair-mosque body carries the name in the same oblique form, unchanged. RECORDED: b4's first reader (observation 41) 'could not tell at once that these are two place names', nor why a commission from elsewhere appears — one reader of the round's three so far; the second half is the source's. The entry stays pending for the reason this ruling gives. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 36, moderate) stopped on the name too — 'one commission or two, and why would a body for two other cities be repairing a mosque here'. Two readers of b4's two; the second half is the source's. The entry stays pending.
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader, checklist item 9: «کمیشن» stands here in the name of a body (ruling N18). Not machine-read: the name carries no quotation marks.

calibration_rulings.title: A named quarter inside a district that already carries the round's district word (Arabic «محلة الرويضة بحي الكوت»).
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat: body and area.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A quarter inside a district is named after the district with «نامی حصے»: «محلہ الکوت کے الرویضہ نامی حصے میں»; the district word is written once. In the area line the town leads as a bare name (ruling P20) and the line ends in the postposition: «ہفوف، محلہ الکوت کے الرویضہ نامی حصے میں».
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the district word stands once in such a phrase.

calibration_rulings.title: The sentence 'in 2017 it was listed among Al-Ahsa's officially registered historic mosques' (jalaniyah here, tahimiyah-e in b4): SHARED-12 of stage 4, changed by round 1 of b3's stage 7.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4: tahimiyah-e body changes its sentence to exactly «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔» — the same string in both batches from its first figure to its stop. Every later page that names the register. ROUND 2: unchanged — the same exact string for both batches; b4's text carries it since b4's round 1 (tahimiyah-e body).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. One Urdu name for the one register on every page: «الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست». The sentence with a year is «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔»; the sentence without one stays «… الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں درج ہیں» (tahimiyah-s). The year stays bare (ruling N12). It is a change of form under ruling P23 — the year, the list, its being official and the mosques being historic all stand — and it is counted under accuracy; A stays on record as the literal wording for the owner. SHARED-12 as stage 4 worded it is withdrawn. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: ADOPTED IN THE TEXT. tahimiyah-e body now carries exactly this sentence (change 1 of b4's round 1, counted from 0), copied by script from b3's jalaniyah body and compared: equal from the figure to the stop. b4's first reader had read stage 4's wording as a circle too (observation 17). The guard holds on b4's text. NUMBERING: in this file, as in b3's, the ids N46, N47 and N48 mean only what b3's judge ruled; the nine items b4's stage 4 had numbered N46 to N54 are N55 to N63 here. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged; the second reader of b4 read the sentence without a remark.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «جو سرکاری طور پر درج ہیں» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the two sentences of jalaniyah and tahimiyah-e are equal by script.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The oasis' on a page whose text nowhere names the oasis ('the depth of learning in the oasis', 'an entire era of the oasis's history').
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat::body, qubba-mosque::body: both leaves were changed in b3's round 2 (its changes 2, 3 and 5), and the sentence of the oasis in each is unchanged. b4: no string of its present text has the word for an oasis; the ruling binds b4, and every later page, only where a page mentions the oasis and no field of it names it. The calibration page and the pages of round 1: not bound as text, and not failed.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C, with the scope the evidence supports. A page that mentions the oasis names it at least once in its own text, in the form rulings P8 and N16 give: «الاحساء کے نخلستان», in the direct case «الاحساء کا نخلستان». Where a source says 'the oasis' on a page no field of which names it, the Urdu names it at that mention: so on bubakr-ribat and qubba-mosque. On a page that does name the oasis, the bare noun and the noun with a demonstrative may stand elsewhere. The ruling is NOT a rule about the first mention and NOT a rule about a summary read on its own: the calibration page (bare noun in the summary, the name at the opening of the body) is neither changed nor failed by it, and no page of round 1 is. B is not taken: it drops the source's noun. No fact enters: the oasis the source means is named, as its article names it. Cost, stated: on qubba-mosque the name lengthens a chain of possessives to four (charged under nativeness on that page). ‖ b5, ROUND 1: met on two pages and applied. kanzan mentions the oasis in summary and body and its source names it in neither: the summary names it, «الاحساء کے نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں», and since round 1 the body's mention carries the name too, «الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان کے مشرقی کنارے پر» (change 4 of round 1; item N75-the-northern-oasis). thulaim's source mentions the oasis three times in the body and names it nowhere: the Urdu names it at the first of them, «شمال سے الاحساء کے نخلستان میں آنے والے مسافروں», and the two later mentions stand as the bare noun. shaban, arbaa and tuwaither have no word for an oasis. The first reader made no remark on the antecedent of the word on either page. ROUND 2: unchanged on both pages. The body's wording on kanzan is item N75-the-northern-oasis's own (the name set before the source's term); this ruling's form is the summary's, which alone meets its guard there. The second reader made no remark on the antecedent of the word either; his doubt of two oases (his item 23) is item N75-the-northern-oasis's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a page of round 2 or later whose text has the word for an oasis has «الاحساء کے نخلستان» or «الاحساء کا نخلستان» in at least one of its fields. This is no test of which mention comes first and no test of a summary taken alone; a check written from it passes the calibration page as it stands.

calibration_rulings.title: The common noun for a governor before a name (Arabic «الوالي العثماني محمد فروخ باشا»).
calibration_rulings.binds: dibs::body. b4: its present text names no governor; the word binds it, and every later page, where one is named.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C. Before a name, a governor is «حاکم». The word of A is not written as a common noun before a name on these pages, because unvocalised it is the everyday feminine suffix and was read so. B is refused under the owner's rule as it stands (P16): a common Urdu word exists, and a reader's preference does not open the door to a loan. Cost, stated: «حاکم» is a shade wider than the Arabic's title (it is also said of a ruler); the adjective before it and the title «پاشا» after the name keep the sense.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on dibs the word before the governor's name is «حاکم», and the only other «والی» of the page is the suffix in «ساتھ والی سڑک».

calibration_rulings.title: The pronouns of the class «جنہیں / انہیں / انہوں / جنہوں / تمہیں»: U+06C1, or U+06BE («جنھیں / انھیں …»)?
calibration_rulings.binds: No string today. b3, b5 and every later text where a pronoun of the four arises.
calibration_rulings.ruling: RE-WEIGHED IN ROUND 2: THE RULING STANDS, NARROWER. A, for the pronouns a text of this site can carry: «جنہیں», «انہیں», «انہوں», «جنہوں», and the forms built on them, are written with U+06C1. What carries the ruling, and is sound: the three outlets this reader reads that gave article text print them with a heh and never with U+06BE (the count does not tell U+06C1 from U+0647: clause (a) of the evidence), the Gulf's Urdu paper among them; the named dictionary heads all three of these words it was read for with U+06C1 (the fourth ruled form, «جنہوں», has no dictionary page behind it (three entry pages were read) and 1 press token on the three outlets against the broadcaster's 5); two blind readers passed the spelling in place; it is the provisional rule under which every page so far was written, and the spelling the stage checker and role file 05 are built for. B is not an error: it is the spelling of the reference site, of one broadcaster and, as far as is known, of the reformed orthography; it is not written on this site. TAKEN OUT OF THE RULING: the fifth pronoun of round 1's list, «تمہیں», with the other forms of the pronoun «تم». Round 1 ruled it with the class; the one reference read for it heads it with U+06BE, no outlet gave a token of it, and under the site's address rule (config: the honorific pronoun only) no text can carry it. It is not ruled either way; if a quoted text ever needs it, it is raised then with this evidence. Ruling P22a is untouched: U+06BE stays where it is a true aspirate. WHAT THIS BINDS: every /ur/ text, interface and pages alike, from round 2 of the line on. No approved string changes, because none carries a pronoun of the class, and no string of b4 does since round 2. Limits of the evidence, stated: three outlets against one, on one morning; one of the two named references unread; the committees unread. On record for the owner, one line: if he prefers the reformed spelling, B is a mechanical change over the four forms, none of which stands on the site today. ‖ THE EVIDENCE, as b4 round 2 measured it: ROUND 2: the entry is rewritten so that it stands alone and says only what was measured. WHERE IT WAS MET: round 1's text of uqair-mosque::summary carried «جنہیں» once, the first pronoun of the class in any Urdu text of the site; two blind readers read the pronoun in that field, the first in stage 5's text and the second in round 1's, and neither remarked on its spelling. Since round 2 that clause is worded with «جن کی» (change 0 of b4's round 2, made because two readers rejected the clause's verb, not for the spelling). So no string of b4, of b3 or of the applied site carries a pronoun of the class today: by the judge's script (b4/s7b-pre.mjs), the four forms and their U+06BE spellings occur 0 times in every Urdu value of the 58 attraction files (11 carry Urdu), in src/i18n/ui.ts, in tm.json and in b3's round-2 text. WHAT IS SOUND. (1) Press, by script on 2026-10-13 (b4/s7-p22-press.mjs, output s7-p22-press.out.txt): on the three outlets from which article text was fetched — urdunews.com (the Gulf's Urdu paper), express.pk, independenturdu.com — these pronouns are written with a heh and never with U+06BE: 12 and 0, 15 and 0, 18 and 0 tokens; on bbc.com/urdu with U+06BE and never with a heh: 0 and 44. (2) The reference dictionary the line's config names, entry pages read by script (b4/s7-p22-dict.mjs in round 1; b4/s7b-p22-refs.mjs in round 2, output s7b-p22-refs.out.txt): the headwords of rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-jinhen, meaning-of-inhen and meaning-of-unhon are written with U+06C1 (the page titles, code point by code point), and those pages carry the U+06C1 spelling 20, 32 and 19 times against 0, 3 and 3. (3) The reference site (stage 4): «جنھیں» 6654 pages against «جنہیں» 104, «انھیں» 29983 against «انہیں» 2273 — B by a wide margin, on a wiki whose spelling is normalised. (4) Two blind readers of this batch read «جنہیں» in place without a remark. WHAT WAS NOT SOUND IN ROUND 1's ENTRY AND IS WITHDRAWN FROM THE GROUNDS. (a) It said '12 with U+06C1': the script counts U+06C1 and U+0647 together (some outlets type the Arabic letter), so its counts say 'a heh and not U+06BE', not which heh. (b) It said 'five outlets of six': nawaiwaqt.com.pk (3 tokens) and dawnnews.tv (2) are too thin to count as outlets, and several of the 'pages' fetched from them and from jang.com.pk were style sheets, images and share links, not articles (the output lists the URLs); jang.com.pk and dunya.com.pk gave no text. The sample is one morning: three outlets with a heh, one with U+06BE, 89 tokens on those four. (c) Gathered in round 1 and not reported: the dictionary's SEARCH page for the U+06BE spelling of «انھیں» answered HTTP 200 and carries that spelling 29 times against 1 — a page that lists what matches its own query, so weak evidence, but it counts the other way. (d) It cited 'the repository's letterform guard' for a set of eleven consonants: the repository's tools/check-ur-text.mjs has no test of U+06BE at all. The set is in the round's stage checker (see the guard). (e) NEW IN ROUND 2, against the class as round 1 worded it: the same dictionary heads the fifth pronoun of the class with U+06BE (entry page meaning-of-tumhen, title code points 062A 064F 0645 06BE 06CC 06BA; 28 on the page against 3 with U+06C1). The dictionary does not spell the class one way. NOT READ, in either round: the Urdu Lughat (udb.gov.pk answered HTTP 500 or not at all, in both rounds on 2026-10-13), which is the other reference the config names; and any page of the orthography committees, whose recommendation is, as far as stage 4 and both judges know, B.
calibration_rulings.guard: WHAT GUARDS THE RULING TODAY. (1) Stage checker, this clause, read from this file by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs on the judge rounds and finals of the attraction batches: none of «جنھیں», «انھیں», «انھوں», «جنھوں» occurs. (2) Stage checker, R/tools/lib/textcheck.mjs, line 48: U+06BE is a finding (code ASPIRATE) after any letter outside its set of eleven consonants (U+0628, U+067E, U+062A, U+0679, U+062C, U+0686, U+062F, U+0688, U+0691, U+06A9, U+06AF). That stops the four banned spellings in any stage file; it would also stop the unruled U+06BE spelling of the fifth pronoun, so the set is part of that question if it is ever raised. (3) THE BUILD DOES NOT TEST THIS LETTER. tools/check-ur-text.mjs in the repository has no rule on U+06BE (its forbidden letters are the eight Arabic letterforms), so a banned spelling in an applied file passes the build today, and only the round's stage checker would stop it on its way there. Whether the four banned forms become a build guard is LEFT TO THE COORDINATOR. For the proofreader, checklist item 1: a pronoun of the four is reported if it carries U+06BE.

calibration_rulings.title: The 'Site status' row of a mosque under restoration (uqair-mosque practical[0]; build check C29, clause d): its Urdu label and value.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-mosque::practical[0].label and ::practical[0].value. The label binds every later mosque page whose source carries the 'Site status' row; the value is this page's alone. b3: no such row.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The label of the status row of a mosque under restoration is «مقام کی حالت»: it says what the English and the Arabic label say, in two words the round has approved, and is kept apart from khuzam's «موجودہ حالت», which renders another source label. The value on uqair-mosque is «بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں»: the subject is the source's (the port complex), the closure stays a possibility, the value ends without a stop (ruling P26), and it does not say whether the mosque itself can be entered. D is not taken: neither source row names the port. FOR THE COORDINATOR, byte for byte from this file: RESTORATION_LABEL.ur = «مقام کی حالت»; UNDER_RESTORATION for uqair-mosque.md, ur = «بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں»; and for RETIRED_IN of the same file the Urdu of the retired body sentence, which is the last sentence of the approved uqair-castle body: «اس مقام پر مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں۔». ROUND 2: LABEL AND VALUE CONFIRMED, byte for byte as quoted above; neither moved in round 2, and the build script compares both with the text. One thing more for the coordinator on RETIRED_IN (the proof pass's finding 17, checked by the judge in tools/check-mosque-card.mjs): the five languages of that table hold only the first clause of the retired sentence ('The site is undergoing restoration work'). The matching Urdu clause is «اس مقام پر مرمت کا کام جاری ہے». An entry made of the whole sentence would not catch that clause written alone; the clause is what the other five entries correspond to. His to choose.
calibration_rulings.guard: Build check C29, clause (d), once its two Urdu entries are filled from this file. For the proofreader, not machine-read: on uqair-mosque the fixed visiting string is absent, the card promises no open visit, and neither summary nor body says that works are under way.

calibration_rulings.title: The title of uqair-mosque, where the pattern of item N43-title-with-a-translated-direction gives two possessives in a row.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-mosque::title.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «العقیر کی بندرگاہ کی مسجد», one pattern with the two tahimiyah titles (item N43-title-with-a-translated-direction) and the port in the form the approved pages write. The body does not call the mosque by its title, as the source does not. Round 1 opened it with a description built on the title's words and the source's 'historic'; the second reader found that sentence circular, the port standing in its subject and again in its place. Since round 2 the body opens «یہ تاریخی مسجد خلیج کے ساحل پر، الاحساء کے مشرق میں، العقیر کی تاریخی بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں واقع ہے۔»: the mosque by a demonstrative and the source's 'historic', the port named once, in the place. C stays on record as the fallback if a later reader trips on the two possessives.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it and carries no Arabic generic.

calibration_rulings.title: abubakr-mosque body: whose house and schools — the Arabic's person or the English's family?
calibration_rulings.binds: abubakr-mosque::body. Any later sentence where the two sources name different owners of one thing.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the English and the Arabic of a field differ on whose a thing is, the Urdu states the Arabic's fact: «شیخ ابو بکر کے گھر اور ان کے دینی مدارس کے قریب». The kunya stands in its citation form because it stands alone as a person's name; inside the page's title, after the word for 'son of', the genitive stays (the two batches' agreed forms, SHARED-10). The first reader's question is the source's defect and is logged for the owner; nothing is added to say who the sheikh is, and the house is not tied to the ribat of b3's page, which no source does. B is on record as the owner's option if the English is the one he keeps.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the kunya is in the citation form only where it stands alone.

calibration_rulings.title: 'A heritage mosque', 'one of Al-Ahsa's oldest heritage mosques': Urdu has no adjective from the noun for heritage.
calibration_rulings.binds: abubakr-mosque::summary (changed in round 1 and again in round 2), abubakr-mosque::body (unchanged). Every later 'heritage' said of a building. b3: its «الاحساء کے ورثے کی پہچان» (qubba-mosque) does not say heritage of a building, so the guard does not reach it; it is neither of the two frames and is not touched.
calibration_rulings.ruling: E. 'Heritage' of a building is said with the noun, never with the word for 'historic', which would make one Urdu word of the two the Arabic keeps apart. As a statement about one building the noun takes its owner: «… ایک مسجد، جو الاحساء کے ورثے کا حصہ ہے». In a superlative frame, the possessive approved on qasr-ibrahim: «الاحساء کے ورثے کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک». D is withdrawn: without an owner the noun was empty to the reader who met it and left the reading of an inheritance open. 'Of Al-Ahsa' in the summary is a word of the page's own body, not of the summary's source: no fact enters the page, since both sources of the body say whose heritage, and it is counted under accuracy as a word from another field. It is taken because the Urdu noun needs an owner in order to mean heritage at all; item N61-district-generic-in-a-summary, which keeps a district's class word out of a summary whose sources lack it, is not moved by this. The owner is one that a source of the same page names (here the body's 'of Al-Ahsa'); it is counted each time as a word from another field; and where no field of the page names an owner, the statement is raised, not completed. The clause «ورثے میں شمار ہوتی ہے» stays withdrawn for a building. B is refused under the role file (a distinction the Arabic makes) although both readers ask for it; it stays on record for the owner as the wording that reads most easily. THE BODY'S FRAME HAS FAILED ITS TEST: round 1 named the next blind reader as its test, and he, like the first, hears it as translated. It is kept all the same, because every remedy either reader wrote is B. Nothing inside this ruling is left to try in the body; the cost is charged under nativeness, and the cure — B, or a source that says what 'heritage' means here — is the owner's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: where the source says 'heritage' of a building the Urdu carries the noun for heritage with its owner, in one of the two frames above. The owner is one that a source of the same page names; it is counted each time as a word from another field; and where no field of the page names an owner, the statement is raised, not completed.

calibration_rulings.title: 'Grammar' as a subject taught beside fiqh.
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::body, abubakr-mosque::body. Every later list of subjects taught in a mosque or a school of religious learning.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Beside fiqh, exegesis or hadith, grammar as a subject of study is «نحو», bare. B beside fiqh reads as 'rules'; C adds morphology and D adds 'Arabic', neither of which the source names. No gloss is added: neither source glosses the word.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word stands only beside another subject of study, never alone in a sentence where it could be read as its homograph.

calibration_rulings.title: On a mosque page, visitors who are not the mosque's: 'visitors to the area', 'the story the old port tells its visitors'.
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-e::body, uqair-mosque::body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as an application of the last sentence of ruling N29: on a mosque page, visitors of a district, a port or any place other than the mosque take neither ruled noun; they are said with the phrase «آنے والوں», tied to their place — «علاقے میں آنے والوں کے لیے», «اپنے ہاں آنے والوں کو». The phrase does not stand bare straight after the noun of the place they come to, where it was read as one phrase with it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the mosque word for visitors stands in this batch in the mosque rows only (five cells).

calibration_rulings.title: May a summary carry the district generic before a district's name when its own source names the district bare?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::summary, umzurainiq::summary. Every later summary that names a district.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The fence is read field by field: a summary carries the district generic where the English or the Arabic of that summary carries it, and stands bare where neither does. Of the two readers who met the bare name, the first did not stumble on it for want of the generic and the second did, as a minor remark. The fence stands as stage 4 applied it: the lack is in both summaries of the source (logged), and half of his doubt, whether the direction belongs to the name, is not cured by the generic, as the body shows; whether a class word set before a name is form in the sense of ruling P23 is not settled here and need not be. B is on record as the owner's option, one line: «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ میں تیرہویں صدی ہجری کی ایک مسجد، …»; the defect of the source (a place named with nothing to say what it is) is logged either way.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no generic stands in a summary whose two sources have none.

calibration_rulings.title: The Eastern Province: the name said in Urdu, or the Arabic name with its article (ruling P1 read to the letter)?
calibration_rulings.binds: umzurainiq::body. Every later page that names the province.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The province is «مشرقی صوبہ», inflected like any phrase («مشرقی صوبے کی مساجد»): an Urdu form in settled use for this province, which is the exception ruling P1 itself makes, and as a name said in Urdu words it has no article to keep — the case of the approved «جزیرہ نما عرب». The country is not named beside it where the page does not name it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the province is written in these two Urdu words, in the direct or the oblique case, and the transliterated Arabic name is not written.

calibration_rulings.title: A district whose English name translates a direction and keeps the rest ('South Al-Rifaa').
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish: summary, body, area. Every later district or village whose English name translates a direction.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the Urdu translates what the English translates and keeps the name with its article (ruling P1) — «جنوبی الرفعہ», with the generic before the whole, «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ». B's adjective carries an article of agreement and a feminine ending that an Urdu reader takes for an opaque word; C drops the article against P1 and goes to the entry for search. The first reader's doubt is the cost of the pattern and is recorded in the entry.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the direction is the Urdu adjective and stands before the name; the generic, where the field's source has one, stands before both.

calibration_rulings.title: The rider of ruling N14 (the page's name does not stand directly against another proper name in the opening sentence), which the ruling words for the fort pages: does it hold for a mosque page?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::body, abubakr-mosque::body (the first sentence of each). b3: nothing moves — jalaniyah and bubakr-ribat open with the place, dibs has an adjective and qubba-mosque a bracket between the two names. Every later page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: CONFIRMED. The rider is not a rule about forts: on any attraction page, where the opening sentence would set the page's own name directly against another proper name, either the place comes first or a comma follows the name; the judge of the page chooses. On hubaish and abubakr-mosque the comma stands, as on khuzam and muhairis. It is not owed where a common noun, an adjective or a bracket already stands between the two names — umzurainiq («مسجد ام زرینیق محلہ العویمریہ میں واقع ہے») and, in b3, dibs and qubba-mosque — and it is not owed where the place comes first. SCOPE (round 2): 'another proper name' is a name a reader can run together with the page's name — of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun that serves as a name and is written bare like any noun («خلیج», ruling P5) is not such a name: «قلعہ العقیر خلیج کے ساحل پر، …» on the applied uqair-castle page is neither changed nor failed by this rule, and no page of round 1 is. uqair-mosque's opening carries no page name at all since round 2 («یہ تاریخی مسجد خلیج کے ساحل پر، …»). ‖ b5, ROUND 1: met on tuwaither and applied with the rule's other remedy. Stages 1 to 5 had the comma after the name, «جبل ابو حصیص، التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں کھڑا ہے۔»; the first reader (his item 41, moderate) calls a comma straight after the subject 'not Urdu punctuation'. The judge of the page chooses the place first: «التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں، جبل ابو حصیص کھڑا ہے۔» (change 18 of round 1). kanzan, arbaa and thulaim open with the place; shaban opens with a clause of its own («آج جس پہاڑ کو جبل الشبعان کہتے ہیں، وہ …»). No opening of b5 sets the page's name directly against another proper name. RECORDED for the rule: on hubaish and abubakr-mosque two readers passed the comma after the name without a remark; here one reader faulted it. Both remedies stay open to the judge of a page. ROUND 2: confirmed. The second reader read the place-first opening and made no remark on its punctuation or its order; what neither reader can picture is a mountain in a quarter north of a village (his item 38), the source's statement in the round's word for the quarter.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: in the opening sentence of a body the page's title is never followed directly by the name of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun used as a name («خلیج») is not such a name. A check written from this passes every applied page as it stands, uqair-castle included. Two things such a check takes from the ruling: a generic that stands before the next name («محلہ العویمریہ») is the common noun between and not part of that name; and the rule is about the page's own title only: a place that is not the page, set against another name with only its generic between (the village in the openings of the two tahimiyah pages), is outside it.

calibration_rulings.title: The Hours value 'Open 24 hours' (Arabic 'open round the clock (24 hours)'): its Urdu on the five pages of b5, and on the later pages that carry the same value (parks, a beach).
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban, kanzan, arbaa, thulaim, tuwaither: practical[1].value (unchanged from stage 1). Every later page whose source value is 'Open 24 hours'.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. TWO FIXED STRINGS for the one English value: «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے» where the page's own name is masculine, «24 گھنٹے کھلی رہتی ہے» where it is feminine. HOW THE CHOICE IS MADE ON A LATER PAGE, without anyone's ear: by the gender field of the termbase entry of that page's own title — the key the title is byte for byte — which is the gender the page's verbs already agree with. The five pages of b5 have «جبل» titles whose entries are masculine: the first string, five times, equal by script. A page whose title's entry is feminine (for instance a title whose noun is «تفریح گاہ», feminine in the termbase) takes the second. Nothing else in the string varies: the figure stays a figure (the number check wants the English 24), «گھنٹے» follows it, and the value ends without a stop (ruling P26). The 24 is a length of time: neither string carries the clock word or a part of the day, so ruling P13 and build check C51 are not touched. The translation memory holds the masculine pair from this batch (five pairs, one string, no note); the feminine string stands in this ruling and enters the memory with the first feminine page; a later stage 1 chooses by the gender of the page's title entry, not by reusing the pair for its English. The value is carried into no other field, and no season, light or advice is added to it. On record for the owner, one line: B, «24 گھنٹے» alone, if he wants one string for every page; and that an Hours row on an unfenced hill, beside two rows that already say open and free, is the source's. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED, LOUDLY, BOTH STRINGS AS THEY STAND — «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے» and «24 گھنٹے کھلی رہتی ہے» — on two readers of the masculine one; they bind the later park and beach pages. FOR WHOEVER APPLIES IT (proof pass, finding 20): on a later page the entry of the page's own title is, until that page's judge approves it, the proposal of its stage 1 — the gender is read from that entry and confirmed by that judge; and a pair of the translation memory has no field for a gender (its keys are en, ur, page, field, date, note), so a pair names its gender only where someone writes it in `note` (the five pairs of this batch carry none), and a tool that reuses a pair by its English alone does not choose between them: the translator of stage 1 does, by the rule above.
calibration_rulings.guard: The five cells of b5 are equal by script (the build script of this file compares them). For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value is one of the two strings byte for byte; its gender is that of the termbase entry of the page's title; the clock word of ruling P13 stands nowhere in it.

calibration_rulings.title: '100,000 square metres' (Arabic in words, 'a hundred thousand'): a figure of exactly one lakh, and a measure rather than a count.
calibration_rulings.binds: tuwaither::body, where the ruled form stands since round 3 (the recorded exception of round 2 is closed). Every later figure of one lakh or more that the English gives in bare digits, count or measure (an area, a length, a capacity, a population).
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE LINE'S FORM IS A. A figure of one lakh or more is written in the Urdu scale, in digits with the scale word, whether it counts things or measures them, and the unit follows the scale word: «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر». This is ruling P10 applied, not a new rule: the scale 'begins at one lakh'; a measure is written like a count (the unit after the figure, ruling N24); the reference corpus writes areas of this size so; and each reader who met the digits converted them. Below one lakh nothing changes («10,000 مربع میٹر» on sahood stands). C stays refused: the figure is a figure. WHAT STOOD IN THE TEXT in rounds 1 and 2, and why: «100,000 مربع میٹر» (tuwaither, body), the source's digits grouped as the English groups them, as the recorded exception of that one string — for one reason only: neither the stage checker nor the build's number guard could then pass a scale word against a bare source figure. The value is the same in both forms and no fact turned on the choice. ROUND 3 — THE EXCEPTION IS CLOSED. Both checks now compare a figure and its scale word by value with a bare source figure of one lakh or more, and the string was replaced by «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر» in tuwaither::body — one replacement, the rest of the sentence unchanged («… کہ 1 لاکھ مربع میٹر کے رقبے پر اس پہاڑ کو …»). THE RULING STANDS AS WORDED: the line's form is A, and no exception to it stands anywhere in the text. The point charged on tuwaither under compliance, and both readers' conversion under fit, were charged for the digits; the page's recorded score is that of round 2 and the replacement does not re-score it.
calibration_rulings.guard: Machine-enforced since round 3. Stage checker (it reads this entry; the opening sentence of the ruling, up to its first quoted form, is what the tools parse and is to be kept word for word): where the English or Arabic carries a bare figure of one lakh or more, the Urdu carries the same value as a figure followed by a scale word of ruling P10; a wrong conversion is a finding, and a figure of one lakh or more left in bare digits is reported with this item's id. Build check on /ur/ (C62): no bare figure of one lakh or more stands in Urdu text, and every figure followed by «لاکھ», «کروڑ» or «ارب» equals, by value, a figure of the page's English counterpart.

calibration_rulings.title: The kicker of a page whose only kicker source is the Arabic «معلم طبيعي» (no English kicker; not rendered today).
calibration_rulings.binds: The five kickers of b5, equal by script. Every later page with that Arabic kicker.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «قدرتی مقام», one string on the five pages and on every later page whose Arabic kicker is «معلم طبيعي». No final stop, no gloss. It stands in no sentence with the largest-oasis claim (C15).
calibration_rulings.guard: The five kickers are equal by script. For the proofreader, not machine-read: a page whose Arabic kicker is this one carries this string byte for byte.

calibration_rulings.title: Al-Ahsa Municipality (Arabic «أمانة الأحساء»): the Urdu name of the body.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, arbaa::body, tuwaither::body. Every later page that names the municipality.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «الاحساء کی بلدیہ», feminine («بنا رہی ہے»; with «نے» the verb agrees with its object), no quotation marks, inflected like any phrase. It is ruling N44-royal-commission-name's build with a common Urdu noun. C is refused by the owner's rule on loans as it stands; B is on record for search. The entry stays pending for one reason: nothing in Urdu attests a wording for this body, and the Gulf's Urdu paper could not be read.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the body is named with the Urdu possessive and the noun «بلدیہ», carries no quotation marks, and takes feminine agreement.

calibration_rulings.title: Two Arabic nouns, a park («منتزه», kanzan) and a resort («منتجع», tuwaither): one Urdu noun or two?
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, tuwaither::body. Every later page that names a resort.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. One Urdu noun whose dictionary senses cover both: a park is «تفریح گاہ», and a resort is said as «سیاحتی تفریح گاہ» with what it offers named in the same sentence. The loan stays out (ruling P16); B's nouns say a tourist site, which the mountain already is.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the resort carries the adjective «سیاحتی» before the noun, and the noun is the termbase key.

calibration_rulings.title: A «جبل» name whose meaning the source itself gives, inside a sentence and for the second word only ("earned its name ('the Four')", "the name — 'the sated one' —"): ruling P3c, case (c), asks for a bracket at the first mention; ruling P3a forbids a bracket after a «جبل» name.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body, arbaa::body. Every later «جبل» page whose source glosses the name.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Ruling P3a governs a «جبل» name: no bracket, in title or body. A meaning the source gives in a sentence is given in that sentence, in the source's place, with the meaning word inside quotation marks as a word cited (ruling N16, point 5). Case (c) of ruling P3c does not reach a name whose generic ruling P3a keeps bare; the guards of P3a and P3c stay as they are. No meaning is supplied where no source gives one («ابا الکباری», «ابو حصیص», «الثلیم», «کنزان»).
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read guards of rulings P3a and P3c as they are. For the proofreader, not machine-read: on a «جبل» page the meaning of the name, if the source gives one, stands once, in a sentence, in quotation marks.

calibration_rulings.title: An editorial gloss that the English sets in square brackets inside a quotation ("'a mountain in Bahrain [the historic eastern coastlands], in whose caves one seeks the cool'"), and that the Arabic does not carry.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body. Every later quotation in which the source sets a gloss of its own.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as a change of form under ruling P23: an editorial gloss that the source sets inside a quotation stands in the Urdu as a sentence of the page's own, straight after the quotation, opening «یہاں … سے مراد», with the content of the bracket and no more. The defect is logged (an editorial gloss inside a quotation, English only; a gloss that does not say of which land), and B is on record as the literal wording. Nothing is added to say whose coast it is.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: nothing stands inside the quotation marks that the Arabic quotation lacks, and no square bracket stands in an Urdu string.

calibration_rulings.title: A second name of a place that both sources set in quotation marks and that carries no Urdu generic ('Aba Al-Kabari').
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::summary, shaban::body (changes 0 and 1 of round 1). Every later second name of this kind. ROUND 2: shaban::body, the fourth mention of the bare cited name (round 2's change 1).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. A second name that the source itself sets in quotation marks and that carries no Urdu generic stands inside U+201C and U+201D at every mention: «“ابا الکباری”». It is one more place for quotation marks beside those the line already has — the three of ruling N16, point 5 (an Arabic phrase kept as a name, a word cited as a word, the short name of a programme) and the translated byname of item N40-quoted-translated-byname; the meaning word of item N70-meaning-of-a-jabal-name-given-in-a-sentence is a word cited as a word, and a quotation proper needs no place of its own. A second name that carries an Urdu generic stays bare, as the approved pages have it. No gloss and no vowel sign: no source says what the name means or how it is vowelled (ruling P17), and that he cannot say it aloud is recorded in the entry. ROUND 2: confirmed for the second name. HOW THE PAGE'S OTHER CITED NAMES STAND, so that the page agrees with its own rule: a BARE name CITED AS A NAME — the name without its generic, spoken of as a name — stands in marks at every mention: «“الشبعان”» four times (the summary; the body three times, the third, «“الشبعان” کا نام اس پڑوسی ٹیلے کا ہو کر رہ گیا», since round 2's change 1) and «“القارہ”» once. A name IN USE, with its generic, stands bare («جبل الشبعان», «جبل القارہ»), as ruling P3a and every approved page have a «جبل» name. Round 1's change log said 'at every mention' while one mention stood bare, after the sources, which quote 'Al-Qarah' and not 'Al-Shaban' in that sentence; the statement is true of the text since round 2.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker, this clause, read from this file by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs: the key «ابا الکباری» in the direct case stands between U+201C and U+201D. For the proofreader, not machine-read: a second name with an Urdu generic carries no marks. Also for the proofreader: on a page that sets a bare name in marks as a cited name, every citing mention of that name on that page stands in marks; a name cited once as a name on a page that marks it nowhere (kanzan's summary) is not ruled here; a name written with its generic stands bare.

calibration_rulings.title: The generic for a town (Arabic «بلدة», 'the town of Al-Taraf'): the word, and its place before or after the name.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body, arbaa::area (changes 9 and 11 of round 1; round 2's changes 5 and 6). Point (1): every later page that names a town with its generic. Point (2): every later mention of Al-Taraf, and any later name that a stage raises as a homograph of a common Urdu word.
calibration_rulings.ruling: ROUND 2: C FOR THIS TOWN, AND THE ORDER OF B FOR EVERY TOWN. Round 1 ruled two things in one sentence; they are told apart here. (1) THE ORDER, for every town: a town is «قصبہ», masculine, and its generic stands AFTER the name, as the round writes «گاؤں» and «شہر»; after a name it inflects like any noun (oblique singular and direct plural «قصبے»). NOT REOPENED: «محلہ» stands before its name, as the approved pages of round 1, b3 and b4 and rulings N45-quarter-inside-a-district, N61-district-generic-in-a-summary and N63-district-name-with-a-translated-direction have it («محلہ الکوت», «محلہ القوع»). (2) THE HOMOGRAPH, which is the case of «الطرف» alone today: the bare name is the Urdu «طرف» with an article, and NEITHER ORDER FENCES IT. The first reader read A as 'the town on the side'; the second read B as a garbled 'towards the town in the north'. Round 1 moved the generic to cure exactly this and did not cure it. Both readers offered the same third form, the first as «الطرف نامی قصبہ», the second as «الطرف نام کا قصبہ»; round 1 had put it on record as the fallback 'if a later reader trips on B'. It is the line's own form for a name the reader cannot take for a name on sight — «سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار» (ruling P3c, point 2), «الرویضہ نامی حصے» (b3, in its body and in its area line). This town is written so at every mention, in body and card: «الطرف نامی قصبہ», «الطرف نامی قصبے کے قریب». The word between says that what stands before it is a name, and adds no fact; the order of point (1) is kept, which is also the order that agrees with the site's «X گاؤں». SCOPE (proof pass, finding 5): point (2) is the rule of «الطرف» and of any later place whose bare name spells a common Urdu word — raised as its own case by the stage that meets it; a town whose name is no such homograph takes the plain order of point (1). WHERE THE SOURCES ARE BARE: the generic is written where at least one of a field's two sources has it (arbaa's area line: the Arabic has it, the English lacks it). Where BOTH sources of a field name a town bare, the case is RAISED to the judge of that page and not completed silently — the fence of items N61-district-generic-in-a-summary and N77-bare-settlement-name-al-qarah; for «الطرف» the homograph is then that judge's ground for completing it, stated in the record. In b5 no field names the town bare in both sources. RECORDED for whoever may reopen the quarter's word: the first reader says the place word stands before one kind of name and after the others, and neither reader of this batch can picture a mountain in a «محلہ».
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word for a town stands after the name it belongs to, inflected before a postposition; the town Al-Taraf has the word that marks a name between its name and its generic at every mention; the word for a quarter stands before its name, uninflected; a town named bare in both sources of a field is raised, not given a generic silently.

calibration_rulings.title: thulaim's area line: English 'West of Al-Oyoun — north of Al-Ahsa', Arabic «غرب مدينة العيون — شمال الأحساء»; the page's own text puts the mountain at Al-Ahsa's northern entrance.
calibration_rulings.binds: thulaim::area. Any later area line whose English can be read as outside the region its page places it in.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the English and the Arabic of an area line differ on a fact, the Arabic is the authority: the mountain is in the north of Al-Ahsa, «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں». The line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition (ruling N30-area-line-without-a-larger-bare-place); C would drop the source's second position. The English wording is logged as a defect of the source, and B is on record as the literal wording.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the line says a part of Al-Ahsa, not a direction from it.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The northern oasis' (Arabic «الواحة الشمالية»): a term the source uses as known and explains on no page.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body (change 4 of round 1). Every later page that speaks of the northern or the eastern oasis.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C. The source's term is kept and takes the name at its mention: «الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان». The owner's name is set before the source's term by this item; ruling N47-the-oasis-on-a-page-that-has-not-named-it's own form is «الاحساء کے نخلستان» with nothing between, and its guard is met on kanzan by the summary alone (proof pass, finding 9). No fact enters. B is not taken: it turns a term of the source into a description and says of the northern oasis that it is a part of the oasis, which this page's source does not say in so many words; it is on record for the owner as the reading that would make one picture of summary and body. The difference between the two fields is the source's and is logged. ROUND 2: C was read by the second reader (his item 23, minor; the first reader's item on the bare term was moderate): 'the second makes me think there is a separate northern oasis'. The doubt is smaller and is still there, and it is the source's on both counts — a term used as known and explained nowhere, and two placements of the massif in two fields. C STANDS; B stays the owner's option.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the term stands with «الاحساء کے» before it at its first mention on a page.

calibration_rulings.title: A list of villages ('the villages of Al-Shu'bah, Al-Kilabiyah, Al-Battaliyah and Al-Jurn'): the generic after each name, as the entries of two of them say, or once?
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, kanzan::area. Every later list of villages, towns or quarters.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. In a list of villages the generic stands once, after the last name, and the plural verb shows the number («… اور الجرن گاؤں اس کے پڑوس میں ہیں»). The entries of «الکلابیہ» and «البطالیہ», which this file does not re-enter, take one line from the coordinator: in a list the generic stands once, after the last name.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a list of two or more villages carries one generic, after the last name.

calibration_rulings.title: The settlement Al-Qarah named bare in both sources ('the palm groves of Al-Tuwaither and Al-Qarah'): the bare word is the second word of the calibrated key «جبل القارہ».
calibration_rulings.binds: tuwaither::body. Every later page that names the settlement.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. ROUND 2: A stands, on the fence of item N61-district-generic-in-a-summary (no generic where both sources of the field are bare); the second reader's remark is logged as the source's, and B remains the owner's option.

calibration_rulings.title: 'His brother Prince Saad fell' (Arabic 'was martyred'): the Urdu verb for a death in battle of a person the page honours.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body (change 6 of round 1, reversed by round 2's change 4). Every later sentence of this kind.
calibration_rulings.ruling: ROUND 2: A. ROUND 1's D IS WITHDRAWN, loudly. Of a person the page names with honour, a death in battle that the English tells with 'fell' is «مارے گئے», in the honorific plural: the plain Urdu for one killed in battle, which says what the English says. WHY THE RULING TURNS: round 1 chose D on one reader and wrote that 'the next blind reader is its test'. The second reader hears D as 'what the news says about accident victims; for a man killed in battle it sounds off' and gives A as the wording that works; the proof pass finds D said 'rarely of one who falls fighting'; the reference counts read at stage 4 and in round 1 go the same way (see the evidence). On register the two readers are one against one — the first found A 'blunt for a prince of a Muslim royal house' — so register does not decide; meaning and usage do. A's cost is on record: to one reader of two it is blunt. B stays withdrawn for the reason stage 4 gave. C, the Arabic's word, is not adopted — the English is the translation source and says 'fell', and the German, Russian and Chinese lines follow it — and stays the owner's option, one line, and the one wording both readers would accept: «ان کے بھائی شہزادہ سعد شہید ہوئے». D stays on record as the wording the first reader expected. A later judge who meets a reader faulting A has this record of both readers, not a fresh choice between A and D.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the verb is in the honorific plural and no benediction follows the name.

calibration_rulings.title: 'A project to humanise the Jabal Al-Arba road' (Arabic «مشروعاً لأنسنة طريق جبل الأربع»): a term of town planning that neither source explains.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body (change 10 of round 1). Every later page that reports a project to 'humanise' a street, a road or a quarter.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D. The planning term is said in plain words: the verb Urdu uses of a road, «بہتر بنانا», with the one thing the term says, for whom — «لوگوں کے لیے». A is withdrawn: its adjective is said of surroundings, not of a road, and failed the first reader. B is not taken: of a road it reads as a mistranslation; it stays on record as the literal. C drops what the term says. Nothing is added about the works (no surface, pavement, lighting or date) or about how the place is reached today; the project is launched, not finished. ROUND 2: D STANDS. The second reader read it (his item 28, moderate, of which he calls the missing access 'more important'): 'vague and sounds translated'. Better than A, which the first reader could not take as Urdu at all, and not cured. The vagueness is the source's: a planning term neither language explains. A plainer wording exists — C — and is not taken, because it drops the one thing the term says, for whom, and the content of a field's source is not traded for a better register, whatever the number of readers (rulings P24 and P25). C is the owner's option, one line: «سڑک کو بہتر بنانے کا ایک منصوبہ». D's cost is charged under nativeness. D still has no count behind it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the sentence names no work done to the road and no date.

calibration_rulings.title: An impersonal verb inside a quotation ('in whose caves one seeks the cool', Arabic «يتبرّد بكهافه»): the Urdu passive, or «لوگ» with an active verb?
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body. Every later quotation with an impersonal verb.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Inside a quotation as outside it, the source's impersonal subject is «لوگ» with the active verb; it renders 'one' and is not a word added to the quotation. No season, time of day or warmth enters with it (C16 untouched).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: nothing inside the marks goes beyond the Arabic quotation.

calibration_rulings.title: shaban's summary: "also called 'Aba Al-Kabari'; the old sources applied its name to Al-Qarah Mountain" — the pronoun follows the second name and does not say which name is meant, in both languages.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::summary.

No fact new to the page enters. The defect is logged and B is on record as the literal wording. ROUND 2: A stands; the second reader's remark is logged as the source's. The rule for the marks of a bare cited name is stated in item N72-marks-round-a-second-name-the-source-quotes.
