calibration_rulings.title: A transliterated name whose Arabic spelling ends in alif maqsura («سلوى», Salwa): the letterform guard rejects U+0649, and the line had no rule for what is written in its place.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body (change 7 of round 1; unchanged in round 2). Every later transliterated name whose Arabic ends in alif maqsura: first «الموسیٰ» (musa-park) and «سلویٰ» (salwa-beach). Not the month «جمادی الاول»; not Urdu dictionary words.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B, as ruled in round 1; REWORDED in round 2 (proof pass, finding 4) so that the ruling, its ground and its guard say one thing. WHAT IS RULED: a transliterated NAME — a name the line builds letter for letter from its Arabic spelling — whose Arabic ends in alif maqsura (ى) is written with «ی» (U+06CC) followed by the superscript alif (U+0670): «سلویٰ». THE GROUND is the identity of the letter, not a count of spellings: Arabic ى and ي are two letters; the letterform guard rejects both Arabic code points; Urdu writes the second «ی» and has «یٰ» for the first, so that without the mark the name is spelled as if its Arabic ended in ya — another name (the first reader read 'salvi'). The mark therefore belongs to the spelling of the name and is not a vowel sign added to help pronunciation: ruling P17, and the reading of it in open item N7, are untouched, and no zabar, zer, pesh or jazm is written on any name. The reference counts in the evidence show that Urdu usage writes such names both ways; they are why the unmarked form is on record for the owner, not the ground of the ruling. WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE: Urdu words whose dictionary spelling carries the mark («اعلیٰ», «دعویٰ», «حتیٰ», «ادنیٰ»). None stands on the site today; the page that first needs one writes it as the dictionary does, and it is no finding under this item. A name with a settled Urdu form of its own keeps that form: the applied «جمادی الاول» is the Urdu name of a month, keyed with its own reference title, not a name transliterated letter for letter, and it is NOT changed by this ruling. WHAT IT BINDS NEXT: «الموسیٰ» for the Arabic «الموسى» in the title of musa-park, and «سلویٰ» again in the title of salwa-beach — each written with the mark from its stage 1 on. The key «سلوی» stays retired for «سلویٰ». On record for the owner, one line: A, the unmarked spelling, which is what the reference site's title for the Kuwaiti place of the same name has.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the retired key is read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs, and the unmarked word standing whole in a text of the attraction batches is then a finding; the marked word is not, the mark being a combining sign the checker counts with the word. For the proofreader, not machine-read: in a transliterated name built from its Arabic spelling, U+0670 stands only after a final U+06CC whose Arabic letter is alif maqsura, and such a name is never written with the bare final letter; an Urdu word whose dictionary spelling carries the mark is not ruled here and is not a finding. Not the month named in the binds, which keeps its settled Urdu form.

calibration_rulings.title: The title of a lake whose English translates the generic ("Al-Asfar Lake", Arabic «بحيرة الأصفر»).
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar, hubail-lake, delfoon-lake: titles and every mention. Every later lake page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A lake is «جھیل», feminine (plural «جھیلیں»), and in a title it stands BEFORE the name, which is built from the Arabic with its article: «جھیل الاصفر», «جھیل الحبیل», «جھیل الدیلفوون». It is the order of the line for a generic that is an Urdu word («قلعہ العقیر», «مسجد جواثا», «محلہ الکوت») and the reference order. The Arabic generic is never transliterated («بحیرہ» is a sea in Urdu). No gloss of a lake's name where neither source gives its meaning. The press order and its two spellings («الاصفر جھیل», «الاسفر جھیل») go into the entry for search and are not written. Where both sources have the name bare (the head of delfoon-lake's body), it stays bare. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on two readers for the generic, the order and the gender. THE NAME «الدیلفوون»: both readers failed to read it (the first saw a slip and other words, the second a rendering of 'dolphin'). The rulings that build a name were read again for a lighter spelling and license none: ruling P1 writes a place name as the Arabic writes it, with its article, and drops only the article of a closed list of settled names; ruling P11 touches only the hamza on alif; ruling P17 adds no vowel sign and no gloss for pronunciation. The Arabic «الديلفوون» has two waws and the Urdu has them. The form stays. FOR THE OWNER, as a naming question and not as a pending decision of the line: whether the Arabic spelling with two waws is the intended one, and how the name is said; a form with one waw could only follow a corrected Arabic spelling. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED on three readers for the generic, the order and the gender. The name «الدیلفوون» has failed THREE READERS OF THREE; the form is the Arabic's and stays, and the naming question to the owner stands as round 2 put it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a lake's title begins with the Urdu generic and is equal to its termbase key; verbs and adjectives agree in the feminine.

calibration_rulings.title: The title of a beach ("Al-Uqair Beach", "Salwa Beach"), and the noun for a beach against the noun for a coast.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-beach and salwa-beach: titles and every mention; salwa-beach::practical[1].value through the title's gender (N87). Every later beach page. ROUND 2: uqair-beach::body, the opening clause (round 2's change 3).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A beach is the compound «ساحل سمندر», masculine, written without an izafat sign; a coast is «ساحل». A title whose English translates everything but a place name takes ruling N43's pattern: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, the generic — «العقیر کا ساحل سمندر», «سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر». It inflects like any phrase («العقیر کے ساحل سمندر پر», «العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر»). After its first mention the beach may be taken up as «یہ ساحل». AMENDED IN ROUND 2: where the source sets the coast and the beach in ONE CLAUSE, the Gulf's shore is said with «کنارہ» — «خلیج کے کنارے کنارے العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر پھیلا ہوا ہے» (round 2's change 3) — so that «ساحل» is not said twice in the clause: both readers read that clause twice (first reader, item 20; second reader, item 16). «خلیج کے کنارے» is approved text for the Gulf's shore (al-uqair body, two interface strings) and stands twice more on uqair-beach and once on salwa-beach. A coast named for itself stays «ساحل»: «العقیر کا ساحل» (the area line), «العقیر کے ساحل پر» (faq[3].a), the approved «خلیج کا ساحل» of al-uqair and uqair-castle. What is left of the cost on uqair-beach, charged under compliance: «ساحل» is the coast in the area line and the last answer and the beach in «یہ ساحل». The press forms («العقیر بیچ», «العقیر ساحل») are recorded for search and never written. ROUND 2: the titles and the generic are confirmed on two readers. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. The clause round 2 amended, which two readers had read twice, was read once by the third; the rule for a clause that names both the Gulf's shore and the beach stands as amended. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. On the published pages this entry is carried by salwa-beach: title, summary, body, and practical[1].value through the title's gender.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title of a beach is the place name's key, the possessive and the two-word generic; the bare «ساحل» is a coast, or takes up a beach already named on the page. In a clause that also names the beach, the Gulf's shore is said with the word of round 2's change 3, not with «ساحل».

calibration_rulings.title: The title of a place named in honour of a person ("King Abdullah Environmental Park").
calibration_rulings.binds: king-abdullah-park::title. Every later place named after a person (parks, a stadium, a street).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A place named in honour of a person is a compound with NO possessive after the person's name, every word translated in Urdu order: «شاہ عبد اللہ ماحولیاتی تفریح گاہ», feminine by «تفریح گاہ» (ruling N69). The king's name follows the entry «شاہ عبد العزیز» and ruling N27 («عبد» in two words; the joined form is in the entry for search). A possessive after a person's name says ownership and is not written; ruling N43's possessive is for a PLACE name. Which King Abdullah is not said by the source and is not supplied. The entry stays pending: no Urdu page names this park, and «ماحولیاتی تفریح گاہ» is attested nowhere. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on two readers. That the noun of ruling N69 is vaguer to a reader than the loan is that ruling's cost and is not reopened; what the park is, the source does not say. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED on three readers for the order and the missing possessive. That none of the three can picture an 'environmental' park is the source's, which explains nothing, and the cost of an unattested compound; charged on the page.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no possessive stands between a person's name and the generic in such a title.

calibration_rulings.title: The label "Visiting" («الزيارة») on a page that is not a mosque (the row of hubail-lake and delfoon-lake).
calibration_rulings.binds: hubail-lake and delfoon-lake: practical[0].label and value. Every later page that is not a mosque and carries a "Visiting" row.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. On every page that is not a mosque the label of a "Visiting" row is «سیر», ruling N17's word for visiting applied to a label; the mosque label «زیارت» is never reused because the English is the same string. The value of the two lake pages is one string, «کھلا عوامی قدرتی مقام، کوئی فیس نہیں», word for word its English ("natural" kept, no "entry" added). C («داخلہ») is not taken: it changes the source's label to fit one value. B («سیر کے لیے») is on record. FOR THE OWNER (source defect): a label that says what the row is about — the row is the fee and the access. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED. Two readers say the label does not tell what the row holds; nor does the English label. For the owner, as before. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. Three readers of three say the label does not tell what the row holds; nor does the English 'Visiting'. Candidate C, which the third reader wrote unprompted, is on record for the owner with the source defect.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the label of a "Visiting" row is the mosque word on a mosque page only (ruling VISITING-ROW) and the word of ruling N17 for visiting elsewhere; the two lake rows are byte-identical.

calibration_rulings.title: "Open 24 hours" on salwa-beach: which of ruling N65's two strings.
calibration_rulings.binds: salwa-beach::practical[1].value.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the masculine string of ruling N65, «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے», byte for byte the pair of the translation memory, because the entry of the page's own title («سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر») is masculine by its head noun. When the batch is applied the pair is entered with the note 'masculine title': ruling N65 observes that a pair of the translation memory names its gender only where someone writes it in `note` (it does not itself ask for the note; proof pass on round 1, finding 21). The feminine string is still exercised by no page; the first park page with this value takes it. ROUND 2: confirmed on two readers. ROUND 3: confirmed on three readers.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value is one of ruling N65's two strings byte for byte, chosen by the gender of the title's entry.

calibration_rulings.title: "North of Al-Ahsa" («شمال الأحساء») on the two lake pages: a part of Al-Ahsa, or a direction from it?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubail-lake: summary, body, area, faq[1].a; delfoon-lake: body, area, faq[1].a — unchanged from stage 4.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE WORDING, ruled for the text until the owner answers: B, «الاحساء کے شمال میں», in the seven leaves. Of the three candidates it asserts least: it is the line's approved build for a direction named after Al-Ahsa («الاحساء کے مشرق میں») and, like the Arabic, is also said of a place in a region's north; A states that the lakes are a part of Al-Ahsa and C that they are outside it, and neither source establishes either. Ruling N74 is not reopened: its ground was thulaim's own text. THE FACT is the OWNER'S DECISION and is not settled here: do Al-Hubail Lake and Delfoon lie inside Al-Ahsa (then «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں» in all seven leaves, one replacement, and the English may say "in the north of Al-Ahsa"), or north of it? With it goes the wider defect: the site uses "Al-Ahsa" for the oasis, the city area and the governorate from page to page. ROUND 2: unchanged; the seven leaves carry one wording and the fact is still the owner's. ROUND 3: unchanged; the fact is still the owner's. RECORDED HERE, in the ruling itself (proof pass on round 2, finding 15): the same Arabic words, «شمال الأحساء», are «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں» on the applied thulaim, where ruling N74 read them by that page's own text, and «الاحساء کے شمال میں» on the two lake pages; the owner's answer evens the two out. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN. The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 5): N88: do the two lakes lie inside Al-Ahsa?
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the seven leaves carry one wording of the position; none says "part".

calibration_rulings.title: A sentence that names two elements of the page it stands on (asfar faq[1].a: "use the “Open in Google Maps” button in the Visit information card").
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::faq[1].a (round 2's change 0). Every later answer that sends the reader to an element of the page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B since round 2, and ONE MORE PLACE for quotation marks, beside those of ruling N16, point 5, and of rulings N40 and N72: the label of a button, a link or a section of the page itself, quoted exactly as the Urdu interface shows it, without its arrow or icon, each label in its own pair of marks. The section is «… والے حصے میں». The element is named with the loan the line has already admitted, «لنک» (termbase entry; ruling P16-test), and the verb is «کھولیں», honorific: «“سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات” والے حصے میں “گوگل میپس پر دیکھیں” کا لنک کھولیں۔» (round 2's change 0). Round 1 had «… کو دبائیں» with no noun: both readers understood it and both said one does not 'press' a link on a phone (first reader, item 18; second reader, item 14; both minor); their own verbs are loans with no entry and are not written. The loan for 'button' stays refused (P16-test): the element is a link that leaves the site, and the English 'button' is said as what the element is. The source's semicolon is a full stop (ruling N33). If the interface string changes, the quotation changes with it. Round 1 called this 'a fourth place'; rulings N40 and N72 of the termbase had each counted a place before it (proof pass on round 1, finding 4), so no count is given here. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. The wording of round 2 passed the one reader who has read it. If the interface round rewords the heading the third reader remarks on, the quotation in asfar's answer changes with it, as this ruling already says.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a quoted interface label is byte for byte the ur value of its key in src/i18n/ui.ts without its arrow; the build has no check that ties the two, and the coordinator is told so.

calibration_rulings.title: Three loan-free forms under the owner's rule on loans (P16) and its test (P16-test): four-wheel drive, caravan, booking.
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::practical[1].value (round 1's change 3). uqair-beach::practical[0].label, practical[0].value, faq[0].q, faq[0].a (round 1's changes 6, 7, 9 and 10), until the owner decides item N100-caravan-loan-or-description. uqair-beach::practical[0].value and faq[0].a for the booking verb (unchanged since stage 1). Every later page that names a four-wheel-drive vehicle or a booking.
calibration_rulings.ruling: The test of ruling P16-test applied to each form, condition by condition. This is the ONE account of it and replaces what round 1 said in three places in three ways (proof pass on round 1, finding 2). (1) FOUR-WHEEL DRIVE: THE LOAN STANDS — «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی», plural «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑیاں»; the cell is «صرف فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی سے». Condition 1 (the native wording is not what the thing is called, shown by the press): met — the Gulf's Urdu paper writes the loan of exactly such vehicles and no native name was found anywhere; the nine-word description was a coinage of this chain. Condition 2 (a blind reader misled): met — the first reader took the native description for any four-wheeled car, on a guarded fact, graded serious. Condition 3 (a dictionary headword OR solid reference attestation): MET IN ITS SECOND, WEAKER CLAUSE ONLY — there is NO dictionary headword; there are five reference pages, two of them running text, and one press page. The test is therefore met as it was for «براؤزر» in b0-ui ('pending: reference attestation only'), and it is NOT the case that all three conditions are met in full: round 1's change 3 and its reader ruling 14 say so in those words and are to be read with this sentence. CONFIRMED BY THE SECOND READER: he read the cell as four-wheel drive only and repeats it in his own words (his items 12 and 36). FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER, because his own rule (P16) is narrower than the test — a loan enters only with an entry that cites a dictionary headword: this is the one loan of the batch admitted on press and reference attestation WITHOUT a headword, and its entry is pending for that reason. If he will have no loan here, the loan-free cell is «صرف چاروں پہیوں کے زور پر چلنے والی گاڑی سے», which a reader took for any car. What decided is the fact: this is the condition he guards with 'only' (build check C37). The figure-and-letter form '4x4' is not written. (2) CARAVAN: the first native description is WITHDRAWN (it reads as a resident's car) and the second, «گھر نما گاڑی» (feminine, plural «گھر نما گاڑیاں»), STANDS IN THE TEXT. What the vehicle is to be called is no longer ruled here: it is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description, with the evidence of both readers and of the press page read in round 2. No third description is coined. (3) BOOKING: THE NATIVE VERB STAYS — «جگہ آن لائن محفوظ کرائی جاتی ہے». Condition 3 is met for the loan (a dictionary headword). Condition 2 is met in its weak form since round 2: the second reader stopped on «محفوظ کرائی» to work out that it means booking, because the same word is the save button and the reserve on these pages; the first reader understood it at once. Condition 1 is NOT shown: the press page read in round 2 writes the loan, but «محفوظ کرانا» is standard written Urdu for reserving a place, and one page that uses the loan does not show that the native verb is not what the act is called. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: candidate B, «آن لائن بکنگ ہوتی ہے», the word both readers say. ROUND 3: unchanged in all three parts. (1) The loan for the four-wheel-drive vehicle is CONFIRMED BY TWO READERS OF TWO and stays flagged for the owner for want of a headword. (2) The caravan is item N100. (3) The booking verb stays: three readers of three would say the loan, one understood the native verb at once, one stopped on it, one finds it stiff, and nobody misread it; condition 1 of the test is where round 2 left it. It goes to the owner with the caravan, as one question about one row. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). الاحساء.source: ur.wikipedia.org — «الاحساء» 156 صفحة وعنوان «محافظہ الاحساء»، ومقابلها 3 صفحات فيها «الاحسا» بلا «الاحساء»؛ urdunews.com — ست مقالات: «الاحسا» بلا همزة ختامية 32 و«الاحساء» 4 داخل عنصر المقالة؛ وسوم الصحيفة: ‎/tags/الاحسا 95 مقالة و‎/tags/الاحساء 84 (قياس المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)
الاحساء.note: P2 محسوم بقرار المالك (2026-10-12): «الاحساء» صيغة رأس الاسم في الموقع كله. «الاحسا» (صيغة اردو نیوز منذ منتصف 2019) تُسجَّل صيغةَ بحث ولا تُكتب في المتن. القراء العميان الثلاثة قرؤوها بلا توقف. P1 محسوم: الأداة مُبقاة. P11 محسوم: ألف مجرّدة لا «أ». P8 محسوم: الوصل بالواحة بالإضافة الأوردية «الاحساء کے نخلستان»، ولا كسرة على الاسم. P20 محسوم: في سطر المنطقة يتصدّر الاسم مجرّداً ثم «،»: «الاحساء، ہفوف کے مشرق میں». لم يُجَب بعدُ: كيف يُكتب سطر العلامة نفسه في /ur/ — يُحال إلى دفعة ui.ur. الجنس مذکر: «الاحساء … کیوں بنا». ‖ ROUND 3, b6: VARIANT FOR SEARCH, never written (ruling N92-governorate-with-or-without-a-gloss): «محافظہ الاحساء», the reference site's title for the governorate under which Salwa falls; the word was taken out of salwa-beach's body in round 1 because a reader read it as another word.

جبل القارہ.source: ur.wikipedia.org — عنوان المقالة «جبل القارہ (سعودی عرب)» = تسمية Wikidata Q12204761 الأوردية (تحقُّق حيّ، المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11: البحث الحرفي «جبل القارہ» = صفحة واحدة هي المقالة نفسها)
جبل القارہ.note: P1 محسوم: يُكتب الاسم كما في العربية بأداته. «جبل قارہ» (اردو نیوز، node/880305، 2024) و«القارۃ پہاڑ» (node/615586، 2021) صيغتان صحفيتان تُسجَّلان للبحث لا للمتن. P17 محسوم: التاء المربوطة «ہ» U+06C1. P3a محسوم: لا گلوس بين قوسين — «جبل» كلمة أوردية (ریختہ: جبل، اسم مذکر: پہاڑ، کوہ)، والقارئ الأعمى عدّ القوس شرحاً للكلمة الوحيدة التي يعرفها؛ فيكفي أن يرد اسم الجنس الأوردي «پہاڑ» منفرداً مرة في متن الصفحة بعيداً عن الاسم. ولا يُجمع الجنسان («جبل القارہ پہاڑ» ممنوع). لا كسرة إضافة على الاسم (P8). الجنس مذکر: «جبل القارہ … سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے».

ہفوف.source: ur.wikipedia.org — عنوان المقالة «ہفوف» = تسمية Wikidata Q27136 الأوردية؛ «ہفوف» 104 نتيجة مقابل «الہفوف» 4 (قياس 2026-10-11)
ہفوف.note: P1 محسوم: اسمٌ له صيغة أوردية مستقرّة بلا أداة (نظير ریاض · دمام · قطیف · ظہران)، و«الہفوف» ممنوعة في المتن. في سطر المنطقة (P20): «الاحساء، ہفوف کے مشرق میں». القارئان الثاني والثالث وجداه غير معرَّف (لا شيء يقول إنه مدينة ولا كم يبعد) — وذلك سكوت المصدر (SD10) لا عيب في الرسم. الجنس مذکر: «ہفوف … ایک شہر ہے».

ارض الحضارات.source: ur.wikipedia.org — شاهد واحد داخل مقالة «جبل القارہ (سعودی عرب)»: «"ارض الحضارات" منصوبے کے تحت تیار کیا گیا ہے» (البحث الحرفي = 1، تحقُّق حيّ، المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11؛ المقالة مترجمة آلياً فهي شاهد للرسم لا للأسلوب). لا ورود في صفحات اردو نیوز المقروءة. والرسم مبنيّ من الرسم العربي الرسمي في ملف المعلم ‖ STAGE 4: not re-counted.
ارض الحضارات.note: P15 محسوم بقرار المالك (2026-10-12): قرية تراثية كما في المصدر الإنجليزي. الصيغة النهائية: الاسم بين “ ” أولاً ثم «نامی» ثم اسم الجنس «ثقافتی گاؤں» — «“ارض الحضارات” نامی ثقافتی گاؤں» — عند أول ذكر في كل حقل يُقرأ مستقلاً (خانة بطاقة، جواب سؤال، المتن)، وهي صيغة القارئ الأعمى الثالث بنصّها. P3b محسوم: گلوس المعنى «تہذیبوں کی سرزمین» مرة واحدة في الصفحة عند أول ورود بترتيب العرض، بين قوسين بعد علامة الإغلاق مباشرةً وقبل «نامی»، ولا يُكرَّر في جواب السؤال. جُرّب إسقاطه في الجولة الثانية فقال القارئ الثالث إن الاسم لا يحمل له معنى، فأُعيد. الاسم بين “ ” في كل ورود. مواءمة مصدر مرفوعة للمالك (SD6): الحقلان العربيان ما زالا يحملان الاسم وحده، ومتن العربية يسمّيه مشروعاً، ولا مصدر يقول أين القرية من الجبل ولا هل تُدفع الرسوم عند المدخل. P11: ألف مجرّدة. الجنس مذکر بحكم «گاؤں». ‖ STAGE 4: b9: the attraction's own page. Title «“ارض الحضارات”» (the key inside its marks, P3b (1); raised as N137); the gloss once, at the opening of the body, «“ارض الحضارات” (تہذیبوں کی سرزمین) نامی ثقافتی گاؤں اور نمائش» (P3b, P15; raised as N136); the four questions carry the quoted key, bare. ‖ STAGE 7 (round 1): b9: Ruled N137 A (title «“ارض الحضارات”», no gloss in the title) and N136 A (the body opens with the name, the gloss once there). Reader item 24 (moderate) found the quoted title a slogan: rejected under P3b, charged. Verified.

ثقافتی گاؤں.source: صيغة القارئ الأعمى الثالث بنصّها («ٹکٹ “ارض الحضارات” نامی ثقافتی گاؤں سے ملتے ہیں»، stages/06c-blind-reader-round3.md)؛ ur.wikipedia.org — «ثقافتی گاؤں» صفحتان كلتاهما لمَعلمٍ من هذا النوع («کٹارا ثقافتی گاؤں»، «کمبوڈیا ثقافتی گاؤں»)، و«نامی گاؤں» 222 صفحة؛ rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-gaanv — «گاؤں — اسم، مذکر» (تحقُّق الحاكم، 2026-10-12: s7-r2-last-out.txt · s7-r3-lookup-out.txt)
ثقافتی گاؤں.note: مدخل الجولة الثالثة (P15)، حلّ محلّ «ثقافتی ورثے کا گاؤں» المسحوب: القارئ الوحيد الذي قرأ ذاك سمعه ترجمةً وأخطأ تقطيع الجملة أولَ مرة. يرد بعد الاسم المقتبَس و«نامی»: «“…” نامی ثقافتی گاؤں». pending لسبب واحد: هو اقتراح قارئ لا نصٌّ قرأه قارئ أعمى في موضعه. الكلفة المعلومة: «ثقافتی» صفةٌ تؤدّي «تراثية» بأقرب معانيها، و«ورثہ» لم تعد ملفوظة. المردود: «ہیریٹیج ولیج» (صيغة اردو نیوز لأسماء المؤسسات، دخيل بلا مدخل معجمي — P16)، «ورثہ گاؤں» (تعليق صورة واحد في ur.wikipedia)، «تاریخی گاؤں / قریہ» (تدّعي قِدماً لا يحمله مصدر)، «تراثی» (ليست أوردية). الجنس مذکر («پرانا گاؤں» 14 مقابل «پرانی گاؤں» 1 في ur.wikipedia).

سعودی ریال.source: ur.wikipedia.org — عنوان المقالة «سعودی ریال» = تسمية Wikidata Q199857 الأوردية (قياس 2026-10-11)
سعودی ریال.note: P7 محسوم: «50 سعودی ریال» عند أول ذكر في كل حقل يُقرأ مستقلاً (خانة بطاقة، جواب سؤال، المتن)، ثم «50 ریال» لما يليه داخل الحقل نفسه. لا رمز لاتيني «SAR» في نص أوردي إطلاقاً — القارئ الأعمى قرأه رمزاً لا ثمناً وعدّ القوس «(SAR)» بقيةً من نسخة إنجليزية. العدد يسبق العملة، و«ریال» لا تتغيّر بعد العدد.

نخلستان.source: rekhtadictionary.com — «نخلستان: فارسی، عربی - اسم، مذکر»؛ ur.wikipedia.org — «نخلستان» 461 نتيجة مقابل «واحہ» 9؛ udb.gov.pk — لا مدخل لـ«واحہ» (قياس 2026-10-11)
نخلستان.note: المقابل الأوردي لاسم الجنس «واحة/oasis». الجمع المباشر كالمفرد والمجرور «نخلستانوں». «واحہ» ليست كلمة أوردية (فخ التعريب). وصل اسم الوجهة بها بالإضافة الأوردية (P8): «الاحساء کے نخلستان». وعبارة «دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان» لا تحمل «کھجور» ولا «قدرتی» في جملتها (قاعدة الموقع C15).

غار.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-gaar-1 — صفحة المدخل: «غار — اسم، مذکر» (تحقُّق المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)؛ udb.gov.pk/result_details.php?word=162657 — المدخل لا يطبع وسم الجنس وشواهده بالصيغتين («بڑے غار میں» 1635 · «گہری غاریں ہیں» 1987)؛ ur.wikipedia.org — «غار» 1877 و«غاریں» 75
غار.note: P12 محسوم: مذکر — جمعه المباشر «غار» والمجرور «غاروں»، و«غاریں» لا تُكتب في الموقع. السند: ریختہ يطبع «اسم، مذکر»؛ والقارئ الأعمى لم يتوقف عند المذكّر، وقال حين سُئل إنه ما يقوله ويكتبه وإن «غاریں» تبدو له عاميةً في نص مكتوب. الاستعمال الصحفي منقسم (اردو نیوز تكتب الصيغتين وتخلطهما في المقالة الواحدة)، فالممنوع هو الخلط. حيث يحتمل اللفظ المفرد والجمع يُظهَر العدد بالفعل («غار ہیں») لا بكمّية مضافة.

پہاڑ.source: rekhtadictionary.com — صفحة المدخل «پہاڑ: اسم، مذکر» (تحقُّق المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)؛ rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-jabal — «جَبَل: اسم، مذکر — پہاڑ، کوہ، پربت» (تحقُّق الحاكم، 2026-10-12، s7-rk-out.txt)
پہاڑ.note: اسم الجنس الأوردي لـ«جبل». P3a: في صفحة معلمٍ عنوانه «جبل …» يرد «پہاڑ» منفرداً مرة على الأقل في المتن بدل الگلوس بين قوسين، ولا يلاصق الاسم («جبل القارہ پہاڑ» ممنوع). «کوہ» لا تُستعمل (صفر في صفحات اردو نیوز الإحدى عشرة، و«جبل احد» 305 مقابل «کوہ احد» 8 في ur.wikipedia).

گوگل میپس.source: ur.wikipedia.org — عنوان المقالة «گوگل میپس» (pageid 986508) = تسمية Wikidata Q12013 الأوردية؛ مطلع المقالة «گوگل میپس ایک ویب میپنگ پلیٹ فارم ... ہے۔ یہ ... روٹ پلاننگ پیش کرتا ہے» (تحقُّق حيّ، المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)
گوگل میپس.note: P16 محسوم: العلامة بالحرف الأوردي كما هي تسمية Wikidata وعنوان ur.wikipedia. ترد في سلسلة الواجهة det.openMaps؛ صيغة هذه المعايرة «گوگل میپس پر دیکھیں ↗» قرأها القارئ الأعمى الثاني بلا ملاحظة، وتُراجَع في دفعة ui.ur. الجنس مذکر بمطابقة الفعل في مطلع المقالة («پیش کرتا ہے»).

فیس.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-fees — صفحة المدخل: «فِیس — اسم، مؤنث» (تحقُّق المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)
فیس.note: P16 محسوم: دخيل مقبول بقرار معجمي صريح — لا مقابل شائعاً له («رسوم» في الأوردو = العادات، فخّ تعريب). مؤنث: «داخلے کی فیس کتنی ہے». الجمع لا يُستعمل في الموقع حتى يُتحقَّق منه معجمياً.

ٹکٹ.source: udb.gov.pk/result.php?search=ٹکٹ — المدخل «ٹِکَٹ»، المعنى 4: «کسی سیر تماشے نمائش وغیرہ کو دیکھنے کا اجازت نامہ جو قیمت ادا کرنے پر ملتا ہے»، وشاهد «اپنا ٹکٹ اوپر بھیجا»؛ rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-ticket-ghar — تعريف «ٹکٹ گھر»: «وہ جگہ جہاں سے ... ٹکٹ ملتے ہوں» (تحقُّق المرحلة 4، 2026-10-11)
ٹکٹ.note: P16 محسوم: دخيل مقبول بقرار معجمي صريح. الجنس مذکر من مطابقة نصّ المعجمين («ٹکٹ ملتے ہوں»، «اپنا ٹکٹ») لا من وسم مطبوع: لم يُعثر على صفحة مدخل للكلمة في rekhtadictionary.com. الجمع «ٹکٹ»، و«ٹکٹیں» لا تُستعمل في الموقع.

سعودی عرب.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article title «سعودی عرب» (pageid 2153) = Urdu label and urwiki sitelink of Wikidata Q851; lead: «سعودی عرب (رسمی نام: …) مغربی ایشیا کا ایک ملک ہے» (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
سعودی عرب.note: Established Urdu exonym for the closed list of P1; the long form of the Arabic is not written. In b0-ui it stands in JSON-LD only (inline.home.country): no blind reader sees it, the proofreader and the judge are its only readers. Gender: the default of country names, NOT read on a dictionary page and not exercised (in the reference lead the agreement is with «ملک»). Shared with batch b1 under the same key. b1: once, in the al-uqair summary, before a postposition; the gender is not exercised there either.

یونیسکو.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article title «یونیسکو» (pageid 27351) = Urdu label and urwiki sitelink of Wikidata Q7809; exact phrase «یونیسکو نے» on 140 pages; urdunews.com/tags/یونیسکو — the paper's tag, same spelling (API and page read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
یونیسکو.note: The organisation's name in Urdu script. Joined to what follows with the Urdu possessive (P8), which agrees with the following noun, not with the name: «یونیسکو کا عالمی ورثہ», «یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے میں». Gender NOT verified and nowhere exercised: the reference lead agrees with «شاخ» («اقوام متحدہ کی ایک شاخ ہے»), and the ergative «یونیسکو نے» shows none; the label is formal. Shared with batch b1 under the same key. b1: four leaves, each time before the possessive («یونیسکو کی فہرست», «یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست»); the gender is not exercised.

عالمی ورثہ.source: built word for word from the Arabic and English term, as role file 04 asks (no Urdu edition of whc.unesco.org); rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-virsa — entry page: «وِرْثہ — اسم، مذکر — مردے کا مال، میراث، ترکہ»; ur.wikipedia.org — «عالمی ورثہ» 67 pages, «عالمی ورثے» 20, «یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے» 8, «عالمی ورثے کی فہرست» 8, against the title form «یونیسکو عالمی ثقافتی ورثہ» (pageid 25904, Wikidata Q9259) and «عالمی ثقافتی ورثہ» 1661; urdunews.com/node/891678 — «یہ نخلستان یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے میں … درج ہیں» (all read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
عالمی ورثہ.note: N2 ruled in b0-ui round 1: this form, word for word the Arabic and English term. «عالمی ثقافتی ورثہ» (the ur.wikipedia title form) is recorded for search and not written: it adds 'cultural', which neither source says, and its oblique contains the string ruling P15 withdrew. Masculine on the dictionary entry page of the head noun; oblique «عالمی ورثے». With the organisation: «یونیسکو کا عالمی ورثہ», «یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے میں شامل», «یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے کا حصہ», «یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے میں شمولیت»; the list: «عالمی ورثے کی فہرست». Read in five strings by the blind reader without a remark on the term. Shared with batch b1 under the same key. b1: in the oblique, «یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست», in three leaves (qasr-ibrahim body and faq[3].a, sahood body); the sahood summary says «یونیسکو کی فہرست», as its source says 'UNESCO-listed'.

Both blind readers of b1 took the bracket for an explanation, not for a second name; the second adds that it says what an Urdu reader already hears in «قصر». b1 round 3: the third reader calls the gloss with the sentence that answers it 'a good touch'; all three ask who Ibrahim was, which no source says.

حساوی لیموں کا باغ.source: built from the Arabic name; no Urdu reference names the farm («حساوی» 0 pages on ur.wikipedia). حساوی لیموں کا باغ.note: Name of the lime farm (a stop of the two-day route in b0-ui). Built from the Arabic name: the English title keeps the nisba and translates the rest, and the Urdu mirrors it; the nisba «حساوی» stands only inside the proper names the site rule lists. The category of farms is ruled «فارم» (N5; «زرعی فارم» in the bar label), and the name keeps «باغ» (a lime orchard is a «باغ») until the round that writes the farm's page settles it. PENDING on one count: no reference form of the name exists. For that round: all three blind readers of b0-ui could not tell whether this is the name of one place or a description; all three found «حساوی» unexplained and set it against «الاحساء کے لیموں» in the line under it; the second and third set «باغ» here against the farm word of the menu. Masculine by «باغ» (dictionary page). ‖ STAGE 4 (b10): the page is written and the title is the key byte for byte. The generic N5 left to this round is raised as N154, recommendation A «باغ»: a lime farm is a citrus orchard (N5: an orchard is «باغ»; the page says «ترشاوہ پھلوں کا ایک باغ»), and P16 admits no loan where the common word exists; home.route.s5.n does not move. The nisba stays (owner's list). Pending: no reference form of the name. ‖ STAGE 7 (round 1): Ruled N154 A: the name keeps «باغ»; N5's 'until the round that writes the farm's page settles it' is settled by this ruling, and home.route.s5.n does not move. The reader could not tell whether «حساوی» is a family name, a variety or a place adjective (item 15, moderate), as the three b0-ui readers: the owner's listed proper name, kept (P6). Pending: no reference form. ‖ STAGE 7 (round 2): Unchanged; the second reader stopped at «حساوی» (item 14), as the first. Pending. ‖ STAGE 7 (round 3): REBUILT on the worktree entry (proof on round 2, finding 1 of should-fix 2): the b0-ui source and note stand verbatim above, the b10 lines appended; nothing else moves. All three b10 readers stopped at «حساوی» (P6, the owner's listed name), none at «باغ». Pending.

Round 1's quoted form was read twice by each of two blind readers and is withdrawn. The word 'site' is not rendered beside the name. Masculine, exercised: «الاحساء کا نخلستان … درج ہوا».

مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا.note: Pending: nothing in Urdu to verify the form against. مسجد الحبیش.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article title «مسجد الحبیش» (pageid 2431941, Wikidata Q99976112), lead «مسجد الحبیش، جسے مسجد شیخ عبد العزیز علجی بھی کہا جاتا ہے، ایک تاریخی مسجد ہے جو سعودی عرب کے مشرقی صوبے، محافظہ الاحساء میں واقع ہے»; exact phrase on 2 pages (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
مسجد الحبیش.note: Named on the jawatha-mosque page; its own page comes in a later round. Feminine by «مسجد».

شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبہ.ar: مشروع الأمير محمد بن سلمان لتطوير المساجد التاريخية
شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبہ.en: Prince Mohammed bin Salman Project for the Development of Historic Mosques
شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبہ.source: built from the Arabic name; press, the short compound exactly as the text has it: urdunews.com/node/758226 (14 Apr 2023) «’مسجد بنی حرام‘ کی تعمیر نو کو شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبے کے دوسرے مرحلے میں شامل کر لیا گیا ہے»; the full name has no fixed Urdu form in the same paper: node/886767 «ولی عہد شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان کا منصوبہ برائے تعمیرِ نو و تزئین تاریخی مساجد», node/758226 «تاریخی مساجد کی تعمیر نو، اصلاح و مرمت، تزئین و توسیع کا منصوبہ», node/563741 «30 تاریخی مساجد کی اصلاح و مرمت اور تجدید و توسیع کے پروگرام»; ur.wikipedia «شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان» 32 pages, «تاریخی مساجد» 359, «تاریخی مساجد کی ترقی» 0; rekhtadictionary.com entry pages «مَنصُوبَہ — اسم، مذکر، واحد» and «شَہْزادَہ — اسم، مذکر — بادشاہ کا بیٹا، شاہی خاندان کا لڑکا» (all read at stage 4, 2026-10-12); b1 round 2, read by the judge on 2026-10-12: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-taraqqiyaatii — entry page «تَرَقِّیاتی — صفت — ترقیات (رک) سے متعلق»; ur.wikipedia exact phrases «ترقیاتی منصوبہ» 26 pages, «ترقیاتی منصوبے» 70, «مساجد کی ترقی» 0
شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبہ.note: The short compound is press usage as written. Since b1 round 3 it stands inside quotation marks, inflected, with its postposition after the closing mark: «“شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبے” کے تحت» (item N16, point 3 a) — the third blind reader's own wording, after he had read the unmarked name as the prince doing something. Round 1's quoted long name had been read as 'the prince of the development of historic mosques'; round 2's unmarked short name is withdrawn. What the project is for stands in a clause of its own with the source's 'for': «یہ تاریخی مساجد کے لیے ایک ترقیاتی منصوبہ ہے». The descriptor says the name's word 'Development' with the adjective of the everyday collocation; the first two readers found «تاریخی مساجد کی ترقی» an odd thing to say of old mosques, and the third calls «ترقیاتی منصوبہ» office Urdu. Pending for the descriptor: the press describes the scheme with words for rebuilding and renewal that the name does not carry. In b1 the key stands in the oblique only. Masculine by «منصوبہ» (dictionary page); not exercised: in «یہ … ایک ترقیاتی منصوبہ ہے» the noun is the common noun and no word shows a gender.

ورثہ کمیشن.source: built from the Arabic name of the body with the admitted loan (ruling P16; item N18 of b1, round 2); no Urdu attestation for this body: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «ورثہ کمیشن» on 1 page, of another body («لوک ورثہ کمیشن», the article on the Lok Virsa museum; counted by the judge, 2026-10-12), Wikidata Q85876178 has no Urdu label (stage 4); the press names this very body with two loans, «سعودی ہیریٹیج کمیشن» (urdunews.com/node/891282, stage 4), the first of which the build guard of ruling P16 bars; for the loan see the entry «کمیشن»
ورثہ کمیشن.note: P16: the name carries a loan admitted in b1 round 2 on the three conditions of the loan test (item N18): the press and Pakistan's own statutory bodies call such a body a «کمیشن»; a blind reader could not tell that round 1's native wording, «ادارہ ورثہ», names a particular body; compound dictionary headwords with the gender printed. The form is the one stages 1 to 5 wrote; «ادارہ ورثہ» is retired and kept for search only. A compound without the izafat sign (ruling P8, point 2); no quotation marks (item N16 as amended). Pending because no Urdu source has this name for this body. Whose body it is, is not said: the source does not say. Masculine by its head word; not exercised («ورثہ کمیشن نے اس کی مرمت کی»: the verb agrees with «مرمت»). b1 round 3: the third reader says the name 'reads like a common noun' and asks whose commission it is; the first had taken it for a body. Kept (item N18); whose body it is stays unsaid.

قلعہ.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-qila — entry page «قِلَعْہ — اسم، مذکر، واحد — وہ سنگین اور مضبوط و محفوظ عمارت جس میں بادشاہ اپنے خدم و حشم كے ساتھ رہتا ہے یا جس میں فوج رہتی ہے، كوٹلہ، حصار»; press: urdunews.com/node/755816 «المعظم قلعہ» (read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
قلعہ.note: The one Urdu word for the English fort / fortress / citadel and the Arabic words behind them on these pages (the English alternates three words for one building). Oblique singular and direct plural «قلعے», oblique plural «قلعوں». Masculine, exercised: «پرانا قلعہ», «ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ». Item N14: the common noun for every «قصر X» of the site, in the summary and at the opening of the body of its page (the first or the second sentence), never next to the name. b1 round 3: on sahood the common noun has a sentence of its own, the second of the body («یہ تقریباً 10,000 مربع میٹر پر پھیلا ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ ہے۔»).

محل.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-mahal — entry page «مَحَل — اسم، مذکر … بادشاہوں، راجاؤں یا نوابوں کا عالی شان مکان، ایوان، قصر»; the reference and the press describe a «قصر X» with it: ur.wikipedia lead «قصر المربع، ریاض کا ایک تاریخی محل ہے», urdunews.com/node/615586 «قصر ابراہیم: یہ پہلی سعودی ریاست کے دور کا محل ہے» (read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
محل.note: Urdu generic for 'palace'. Since item N14 (b1 round 1) it stands in no title: an Arabic «قصر» keeps its own generic («قصر صاہود»). In the text only on qasr-ibrahim, in the gloss and in the sentence that answers it: «قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل)», «یہ عیش و عشرت کا محل نہیں بلکہ ایک قلعہ ہے». Never placed next to a name that keeps the Arabic generic. Two blind readers took «X محل» for a royal palace. Masculine, exercised. ‖ b7, ROUND 1 (item N113): a second place in the text — the summary of mushaqar, «اس کے قلب میں ایک محل ہے جو اسی قلعے سے متاثر ہو کر بنایا گیا», where both sources have the bare common noun 'a palace'. The building's NAME on that page keeps the Arabic generic, in marks («“قصر المشقر”»), and the Urdu word never stands next to it. The first reader of b7 notes the two words for one building (his item 40). ‖ STAGE 7 (round 2): b7, ROUND 2: the second reader, like the first, notes the two words for one building on mushaqar (his item 38).

مدرسہ.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-madrasa — entry page «مَدْرَسَہ — اسم، مذکر، واحد — درس دینے یا پڑھانے کی جگہ، جائے درس، پڑھانے کی جگہ، اسکول، مکتب، تعلیم گاہ»; its English-headword page 'school' gives «درس گاہ، مَدْرَسَہ، مَکتَب»; ur.wikipedia — the article for 'school' is titled «مدرسہ» (pageid 5331, Wikidata Q3914) and the title «اسکول» redirects to it; «سرکاری مدرسہ» 67 pages against «سرکاری اسکول» 120 (all read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
مدرسہ.note: Item N15 ruled in b1 round 1: «مدرسہ» is written inside names («مدرسہ امیریہ»; as «مدرسہ صولتیہ» in the reference) and is the word for a religious seminary; a school of general education is «اسکول». The first blind reader of b1 read «پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری مدرسہ» as the first regular government seminary, the second read the title «مدرسہ امیریہ» so until the next line, and the reader's paper uses the word for seminaries only. As a common noun it does not stand in the text of this batch; inside the name it is glossed once on the name's own page (P3c, case 1b). Masculine; oblique «مدرسے». The third blind reader took the title for a seminary as well, until the summary and the gloss.

تفریح گاہ.source: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-tafriih-gaah — entry page «تَفْرِیح گاہ — فارسی، عربی - اسم، مؤنث — سیر تماشے کی جگہ ، تفریح کا مقام» (read at stage 4, 2026-10-12); the interface batch's log: Urdu Lughat defines the loan itself through this word («پارْک — آبادی کے اندر یا اس سے متصل وہ تفریح گاہ …»)
تفریح گاہ.note: P16: the native word is written, not the loan; the interface batch uses the same word in its category label and navigation. It will carry the titles of the park pages of later rounds. Feminine, exercised: «تفریح گاہ … کھلی رہتی ہے», «ساتھ والی تفریح گاہ». Since b1 round 1: one wording for the park beside the mosque in its four leaves, «ساتھ والی تفریح گاہ» (the card label, one question and both answers), where the text had followed the English's 'adjacent' and 'beside'; the second reader passed it. b1 round 3: all three blind readers of b1 ask what kind of place is meant beside the mosque (a park, a garden, rides), and b2's third asks the same of the one beside its fort: the Arabic's word is as wide, and no body describes the place. Recorded for the round that writes a park page; the loan the readers have in mind would have to pass the loan test of ruling P16 there.

شندل.source: built from the Arabic spelling; ur.wikipedia exact phrase on 2 pages: the article «قصر ابراہیم» («چھتیں کھجور کے درخت کی لکڑی، شندل اور پتھروں سے بنائی گئی ہیں» — a machine-translated article: evidence of the spelling only) and a village in Iran (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12); no dictionary page was looked for
شندل.note: Pending: one attestation of the spelling in a machine translation, no dictionary entry, gender unverifiable. Explained in place and only in the source's words (owner ruling, build check C40). Since b1 round 2: «شندل نامی لکڑی (جو کبھی خلیجی خطے میں درآمد کی جاتی تھی)» — the generic follows the name after «نامی», because both blind readers of b1 took the bare word for a misprint of the word for sandalwood, and the import is said of the region with the adjective of ruling P5, because 'imported into the Gulf' read as an odd thing to say. What the wood is and where it came from are not in the owner-ruled explanation and are not added (logged with the source observations). Gender by the word written with it, «لکڑی» (feminine): «درآمد کی جاتی تھی». b1 round 3: the third reader took it for a misprint of sandalwood too, with «نامی لکڑی» beside it: three readers of three. No wording can part the two words; only a fact the source lacks (which wood, from where) could, or a vowel mark, which ruling P17 bars.

خندق.source: usage, against the printed dictionary label. rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-khandaq — entry page prints «خَنْدَق — اسم، مذکر — گہری کھدی ہوئی زمین جو شہر، مکان قلعے وغیرہ کے چاروں طرف حفاظت کے لیے … کھودی گئی ہو»; ur.wikipedia exact phrases: «خندق کھودی» 17 pages against «خندق کھودا» 0, «گہری خندق» 7 against «گہرا خندق» 0, «خندق بنائی» 3 against «خندق بنایا» 0, «خندق تھی» 1 and «خندق تھا» 1; udb.gov.pk could not be reached (stage 4, 2026-10-12)
خندق.note: NEW at stage 4: the text exercises the gender («کبھی اس کے گرد ایک دفاعی خندق ہوا کرتی تھی», sahood body) and stage 1 had written it from the translator's own knowledge. Written feminine, as reference usage has it 27 to 0 in the three frames that show agreement; pending because the one dictionary label that could be read says masculine — the same case as «بندرگاہ». A wording that shows no gender is on record for the judge: «اور کبھی یہ ایک دفاعی خندق سے گھرا ہوا تھا». The plural is not used in the text and was not read on a dictionary page.

اسکول.source: rekhtadictionary.com — entry pages of compound headwords, read by the judge on 2026-10-12: meaning-of-private-school «پِرائیویٹ اِسْکُول — اسم، مذکر — وہ اسکول جسے گورنمنٹ نے قائم نہ کیا ہو بلکہ کسی فرد یا غیر سرکاری جماعت نے قائم کیا ہو», meaning-of-public-school «پَبْلِک اِسْکُول — اسم، مذکر», meaning-of-middle-school «مِڈِل اِسکول — … وہ اسکول جہاں آٹھویں درجے تک تعلیم دی جاتی ہے», meaning-of-night-school; six more compound headwords in the dictionary's search list; its entries «مَدْرَسَہ» and «درس گاہ» define their words with it. NO entry page of the bare headword was found (three slugs redirect to the home page) and udb.gov.pk could not be reached (two requests failed). For the thing — Chrome's Urdu resources: «اسکول» 11 times in generated_resources_ur.xtb and 5 in components_strings_ur.xtb («اسکول کا اکاؤنٹ», «آپ کا آجر یا اسکول»), «مدرسہ» not once; ur.wikipedia: article title «سرکاری اسکول», «سرکاری اسکول» 120 pages against «سرکاری مدرسہ» 67, «اسکول میں» 4523 against «سکول میں» 29; press: urdunews.com/tags/اسکول — «نجران کا قدیم تاریخی سکول جہاں چھ طلبا او تین اساتذہ تھے» (node/897134), «ظھران میں 77 برس قدیم سکول کی نایاب تصویر» (node/501776), «نجی سے سرکاری سکولوں میں ٹرانسفر کا طریقہ مقرر» (node/758391)
اسکول.note: P16: a loan admitted in b1 round 1 on the three conditions of the loan test (item N15) — the press and the browser do not call a school of general education «مدرسہ» (the reader's paper keeps that word for seminaries and sets it against «سکول»: urdunews.com/node/750771, node/626136); the blind reader read «سرکاری مدرسہ» as a government seminary (observation 43, serious); compound headwords with the gender printed. The COMMON NOUN only: names keep «مدرسہ» («مدرسہ امیریہ»). Spelled with the alif, as the dictionary heads it and the reference site and the browser write it; the press spelling of the Kingdom, «سکول», is recorded for search and not written. Masculine on two entry pages, exercised: «پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا»; plural «اسکول», oblique plural «اسکولوں». Verified for form and gender on compound headwords; a page for the bare headword is still to be found. Read blind in b1 round 2 in its three sentences, without a remark; since round 2 it also stands in the gloss of the school's name, «مدرسہ امیریہ (یعنی امیریہ اسکول)». Read by a third reader in its four places without a remark.

کمیشن.en: commission (in the name of a body)
کمیشن.source: rekhtadictionary.com — entry pages of compound headwords, read by the judge in b1 round 1 (2026-10-12): «تَحْقِیْقاتی کَمِیشَن — انگریزی، عربی - اسم، مذکر — معتبر اور ما ہرین کی جماعت …», «مُعائِنَہ کَمِیشَن — اسم، مذکر — جانچ پڑتال کرنے والی مقرر کردہ مجلس یا جماعت»; NO entry page of the bare headword was found (three slugs redirect to the dictionary's home page, the third tried in round 2) and udb.gov.pk could not be reached; ur.wikipedia exact phrase «الیکشن کمیشن» on 1650 pages (round 1); press: «سعودی ہیریٹیج کمیشن» (urdunews.com/node/891282, stage 4)
کمیشن.note: P16: a loan admitted in b1 round 2 on the three conditions of the loan test (item N18), for the NAME of a body that is called a commission («ورثہ کمیشن»); as a common noun the Urdu word is «ادارہ». Masculine on two entry pages of compound headwords; not exercised in the text. The direct plural equals the singular, oblique plural «کمیشنوں»; neither is used in the text and neither was read on a dictionary page. Verified for form and gender on compound headwords; a page for the bare headword is still to be found.

جزیرہ نما عرب.en: the Arabian Peninsula (the sources of b1: 'the peninsula')
جزیرہ نما عرب.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article title «جزیرہ نما عرب» (pageid 12374), lead «جزیرہ نمائے عرب یا عربستان …»; the title phrase on 768 pages and «جزیرہ نما عرب کے» on 127, against «جزیرہ نمائے عرب» on 52; rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-jaziira-numaa — entry page «جزیرہ نُما — اسم، مذکر» (API and page read by the judge, 2026-10-12)
جزیرہ نما عرب.note: NEW in b1 round 2. Both sources of al-uqair say 'the heart of the peninsula', and both blind readers of b1 found the bare «جزیرہ نما» unfinished in Urdu ('we name the peninsula'). The name is written in the form of the reference title, without the izafat ending of the variant «جزیرہ نمائے عرب» (ruling P8). It brings in no fact: the Arabic's word with its article is this peninsula and no other. Masculine on the dictionary page of the head word; not exercised («جزیرہ نما عرب کے قلب تک»). Read by the third reader without a remark.

قصر محیرس.source: built from the Arabic name as it stands (item N14, ruled in b1 round 1 for both attraction batches); its generic is an Urdu dictionary word in the sense of the English title — rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-qasr-1, entry page «قَصْر — اسم، مذکر», third sense «ایوان، محل، بارگاہ» (read by b1's stage 4 and again by b1's judge, 2026-10-12); the pattern is that of the reference titles for Saudi palaces: «قصر ابراہیم» (pageid 2444298), «قصر خزام» (pageid 1090950), «قصر المربع» (pageid 2425880) (b1's stage 4); NO Urdu attestation of this name in any form: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «قصر محیرس» 0 pages (re-counted by this judge, 2026-10-12), «محیرس» 0, «محیرس محل» 0, «قلعہ محیرس» 0 (stage 4); Wikidata Q12233066 (en 'Muhaires Castle') has no Urdu label and no urwiki sitelink (stage 4)
قصر محیرس.note: Item N14 (ruled in b1 round 1, kept in its round 2; applied here since round 1): «قصر X» is the one form for an Arabic «قصر» whose English title says 'Palace', in title and body; no labelled bracket and no gloss. Replaces the stage-1 key «محیرس محل», which is retired and kept for search only: the first blind reader took that title for a royal palace ('I would have told the family we are going to see a palace') of a watch fort twenty metres a side. PROOFED AND READ BLIND in this form (round 2): the second reader opened the page 'expecting a palace and was told at once it is a small watch-fort' — the cost the ruling states, put right by the page's next line; he asks why no «قصر» name is explained, which item P3c answers. The common noun «قلعہ» stands in the summary and in the second sentence of the body («یہ ایک چھوٹا سا قلعہ ہے جو نگرانی اور پہرے کے لیے بنا تھا۔»), never next to the name. Since round 2 a comma follows the name in the opening sentence («قصر محیرس، المبرز کے شمال میں واقع ہے۔»: the rider to item N14), because the second reader read the fort's name and the town's as one name. Pending for one reason: nothing in Urdu names the fort. Never doubled («قصر محیرس محل»). Masculine by «قصر» (dictionary page); the forms of the text that inflect for it: «یہ کچی اینٹوں اور پتھر سے بنا ہے», «یہ نگرانی کی چوکی کا کام دیتا تھا». Neither reader could tell how «محیرس» is said; no vowel mark is written (ruling P17). b2 round 3: unchanged. The third reader, like the second, says that «قصر» is a palace in Urdu and that 'nothing tells me «قصر» is simply part of the local name' (moderate); he read the opening with its comma without running the names together. Three readers of three cannot say «محیرس» aloud.

قصر خزام.source: built from the Arabic name as it stands (item N14, ruled in b1 round 1); its generic is an Urdu dictionary word in the sense of the English title — rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-qasr-1, entry page «قَصْر — اسم، مذکر», third sense «ایوان، محل، بارگاہ» (b1's stage 4 and judge, 2026-10-12). HOMONYM: the ur.wikipedia article titled «قصر خزام» (pageid 1090950, Wikidata Q6172700) is the palace of the same name in JEDDAH (lead «قصر خزام … سعودی عرب کا ایک عجائب گھر ہے»); the exact phrase stands on 2 pages, both that palace (re-counted by this judge, 2026-10-12); nothing in Urdu names the fort of Hofuf in any form («قلعہ خزام» 0 pages, «خزام محل» 1 page: the Jeddah palace; stage 4); Wikidata Q12233036 (en 'Khuzam Palace, Al-Ahsa') has no Urdu label and no urwiki sitelink (stage 4)
قصر خزام.note: Item N14 (b1 rounds 1 and 2), applied here since round 1, as «قصر محیرس». Replaces the stage-1 key «خزام محل», retired and kept for search only. Pending on two counts: no Urdu source names this fort, and an Urdu search for the name finds the palace in Jeddah — the page's summary and first body sentence place this one in Hofuf. PROOFED AND READ BLIND in this form (round 2): the second reader met a palace in the title and a fort in the next line, as on muhairis. The common noun «قلعہ» stands in the summary and in the second body sentence («یہ قلعہ 1220 ہجری … تعمیر کیا»). Since round 2 the name is set off by a comma in the opening sentence, in the second reader's own words («قصر خزام، ہفوف کے مغرب میں، محلہ المزروعیہ کے کنارے واقع ہے۔»: the rider to item N14). Masculine by «قصر»; the form of the text that inflects for it: «یہ ان قلعوں کے سلسلے کی ایک کڑی تھا». Never doubled. Neither reader could tell how «خزام» is said (ruling P17), and both stopped at the sentence that derives the name from «زمام» (see that entry). b2 round 3: unchanged as a name. The third reader read the opening with its two commas without a stumble. The summary now reads «… ایک قلعہ۔ یہ الاحساء کے نخلستان کا حصہ ہے، جو یونیسکو کی فہرست میں شامل ہے۔», his own words, so that the listing is not attached to the fort before the oasis is named. Three readers of three stopped at the sentence that derives the name from «زمام».

بیت البیعہ.source: built from the Arabic spelling (ruling P1: article kept; P17: the final letter as U+06C1); no Urdu attestation: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «بیت البیعہ» 0 pages, no such title; Wikidata Q99677807 (ar «بيت البيعة», en 'House of Allegiance') has no Urdu label and no urwiki sitelink (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12); gender by the generic in the sense 'house': rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-bait-1 — entry page «بَیْت — اسم، مؤنث: شعر …؛ اسم، مذکر: گھر، مکان», and rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-ghar-6 — «گَھر — اسم، مذکر» (both read at stage 4)
بیت البیعہ.note: Pending: nothing in Urdu to verify the form against. The title mirrors title_en (the transliteration is kept). The English body itself glosses the name ('the House of Allegiance'), so the page's own name takes the gloss once, at its first mention in the body, in the form item P3c rules (b1 rounds 1 and 2; adopted): «بیت البیعہ (یعنی بیعت کا گھر)»; it stands bare in the title, the path line and the picture labels. The gloss field stays empty on purpose: a filled gloss would make this a P3b name that must stand inside quotation marks at every mention, which a page title cannot do — the difference from b1's «بیت الثقافہ». Both blind readers took «البیعہ» in the title first from the word for a sale, and both say the bracket puts it right (the first: it 'clears it at once'; the second: 'the explanation in brackets is good', though it comes after the title and the summary). Masculine by the dictionary's 'house' sense of «بیت»; not exercised («… میں ہے», «… معروف ہے»). b2 round 3: the third reader, as the two before him: in the title the word is first read from the word for a sale, and the bracket 'clears it up at once and its purpose is plain'.

بیت الملا.source: built from the Arabic spelling (ruling P1); no Urdu attestation: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «بیت الملا» 0 pages (API, counted at stage 4, 2026-10-12); the family name as b1's adopted entry «مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا» writes it
بیت الملا.note: Pending: nothing in Urdu to verify the form against. The second name of the house, given once: «… بیت الملا کے نام سے بھی معروف ہے». «بھی» is a repair of form under ruling P23, made in round 1: the source says 'known as', and the first blind reader could not tell which of the two names is in use; the literal wording is on record («بیت الملا کے نام سے معروف ہے»). Not glossed: the summary, which renders first, has already said «الملا خاندان کا تاریخی گھر». The first reader read the name for a moment as 'the mullah's house'; the second read the sentence without a remark. Gender as «بیت البیعہ»; not exercised. b2 round 3: the third reader read the name for a moment as 'the mullah's house' and finds «معروف» stiff where he would say «مشہور», which says 'famous' and is not taken.

الملا خاندان.source: built from the Arabic family name with its article, as b1's adopted entry «مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا» writes it, and the Urdu word for family that ruling P16 prescribes; the exact phrase stands on 0 pages of ur.wikipedia; the reference site names this family «آل ملا» (2 pages, one of them the lead of the article on its scholar, pageid 2484151) and once «آل الملا»; gender: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-khaandaan — entry page «خانْدان — اسم، مذکر — گھرانا، قبیلہ، کنبہ» (all read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
الملا خاندان.note: Pending: the compound is built and stands on no Urdu page. Stands in the summary («الملا خاندان کا تاریخی گھر») and in the body («وہ الملا خاندان کے بزرگ، فقیہ اور قاضی تھے۔»). The reference form «آل ملا» is recorded for search. Masculine by the dictionary's label; not exercised: the possessive in «الملا خاندان کا تاریخی گھر» agrees with «گھر», and no word of the text agrees with «خاندان» (corrected in round 3 on finding 12 b of the proof pass). The second had no remark on the name. b2 round 3: the third reader, like the first, read it for a moment as 'the mullah's family'.

شیخ عبد الرحمن بن عمر بن محمد الملا.note: Pending: nothing in Urdu names this judge. REPLACES the stage-1 key, which wrote the name joined (decision of item N27; the joined spelling is the Arabic file's and is recorded for search). The blind reader asked whether he is the Abdulrahman in the name of the later scholar; no source says. b2 round 2: the second blind reader asked the same as the first — the next scholar's «بن عبد الرحمن» 'made me take him for the builder's son', born 65 years after the house was built; no source says. b2 round 3: the third reader asked the same; three readers of three.

عبد اللطیف بن عبد الرحمن الملا.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article «عبد اللطیف بن عبد الرحمن ملا» (pageid 2484151, Wikidata Q99677480), found at stage 4 (stage 1 had not found it); its lead names him with the family's «آل ملا», gives the years 1853–1921 and calls him «ایک ممتاز حنفی فقیہ، قاضی اور دینی مدرس»; the same article has «ہفوف کے محلہ الکوت میں ایک علمی خاندان میں پیدا ہوئے»; exact phrases: «عبد اللطیف بن عبد الرحمن» 12 pages (other bearers among them), «عبداللطیف بن عبدالرحمن» 0 (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
عبد اللطیف بن عبد الرحمن الملا.note: Verified: the person, his years (1853–1921), his standing as jurist and judge and the spelling of each element are confirmed by the reference article, and the one point the entry waited for is ruled (item N27, b1 round 1, kept in its round 2): the family name keeps its article, as the Arabic writes it, where the reference title drops it («… ملا», recorded for search) — so that the family has one name on the page and in the round (b1's «مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا»). REPLACES the stage-1 key (joined spelling). Followed in the body by his years, «(1853–1921)», bare as both sources leave them and with the en dash b1's item N13 keeps for a bracketed lifespan; both blind readers had to guess what the two years are. Since round 2 what is said of him is a sentence of its own, with the honorific plural: «وہ الملا خاندان کے بزرگ، فقیہ اور قاضی تھے۔» (the second reader had first read the relative «جو» as the house). Both readers asked whether he is the builder's son; no source says. b2 round 3: the third reader read the sentence on him without attaching its pronoun to the family; he notes that the bracketed years are not labelled and carry no calendar word.

شاہ عبد العزیز.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article «عبد العزیز بن عبد الرحمن آل سعود» (pageid 5790, Wikidata Q151509), to which the titles «شاہ عبدالعزیز» and «عبدالعزیز ابن سعود» redirect; exact phrase «شاہ عبد العزیز» on 534 pages (led by the Delhi scholar of the same name and by «شاہ عبد العزیز یونیورسٹی»; for this king e.g. the article «جدہ»: «شاہ عبد العزیز کے لیے نئے خزام محل کی تعمیر کی گئی»), the joined «شاہ عبدالعزیز» on 68; the Urdu label of the Wikidata item is joined («عبدالعزیز ابن سعود»). شاہ عبد العزیز.note: REPLACES the stage-1 key, which wrote the name joined. «شاہ» is the Urdu title for a king before the name. The name is written in two words, as the reference title and the majority of the reference site write it and as the round's adopted «بنو عبد القیس» writes the same construction; the joined form — the Arabic file's and the press's — is recorded for search and not written (item N27). Honorific plural: «شاہ عبد العزیز … پہنچے تو … داخل ہوئے», «ان کے ہاتھ پر بیعت کی». b2 round 1: the blind reader would write the name joined ('with the gap they look lifted from an Arabic page'): recorded as an owner option under item N27, not applied. He asked how this king relates to the Saud bin Abdulaziz of the two fort pages; no page says. b2 round 2: the second blind reader, as this entry foresaw: with «بیعت» the name 'first calls up the Delhi scholar of that name; the year and الاحساء correct it at once'. The page never says who the king is: the source's. b2 round 3: the third reader says the king is 'brought in as someone I am expected to know', which is the source's; he too would write the names with «عبد» joined, and calls it taste. Round 2: two blind readers first took the name for the Delhi scholar of the same name and connected it with the king only from the context; the key is not reopened, and a sentence that needs the king a second time writes the key whole, never the bare first word.

سعود بن عبد العزیز.source: ur.wikipedia.org — article «سعود بن عبد العزیز بن محمد بن سعود» (pageid 675329) = Urdu label and urwiki sitelink of Wikidata Q2227089; lead «… جسے عام طور پر سعود الکبیر کے نام سے جانا جاتا ہے پہلی سعودی ریاست کا 1803ء سے 1814ء تک حکمران تھا»; exact phrase «سعود بن عبد العزیز» on 38 pages, the first of them that article; the joined «سعود بن عبدالعزیز» on 63, most of them the king of 1953–1964, whose own article is titled joined («سعود بن عبدالعزیز آل سعود», pageid 19046) (API, read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)

One person, two title treatments, as the two pages have them: muhairis (1208 AH) «سعود بن عبد العزیز نے …، جو بعد میں امام بنے»; khuzam (1220 AH) «امام سعود بن عبد العزیز … جو پہلی سعودی ریاست کے تیسرے امام تھے» — consistent with the reference lead (ruler from 1803). The epithet «سعود الکبیر» of the reference is not written: neither source has it. Honorific plural agreement on both pages. b2 round 1: two remarks of the blind reader, both the source's: «جو بعد میں امام بنے» was read as 'he later became a prayer leader' (neither page says that 'Imam' is the ruler's title here), and beside the year 1794 the name made him think of a king of recent times. Homonym for search and for the proofreader: the king of 1953 to 1964, whose reference title is written joined. b2 round 2: the second blind reader made both remarks of the first — he read «امام بنے» first as becoming the imam of a mosque or a religious leader, and the name is a twentieth-century king's to him; he points to khuzam's wording as the one that cannot be misread. Two readers of two; the source's, with an option on record for the owner («جو بعد میں اسی ریاست کے امام بنے»). b2 round 3: the third reader made both remarks again. Three readers of three; the source's.

پہلی سعودی ریاست.source: ur.wikipedia.org — exact phrase «پہلی سعودی ریاست» on 28 pages, among them the lead of the article on the imam of these two pages («… پہلی سعودی ریاست کا 1803ء سے 1814ء تک حکمران تھا») and the article «وہابی جنگ» («امارت درعیہ (پہلی سعودی ریاست) کی افواج»); the article for the state itself is titled «امارت درعیہ» (pageid 88958 = Urdu label of Wikidata Q146871), whose lead gives the Arabic name «الدولة السعودية الأولى»; press: urdunews.com/node/615586 «قصر ابراہیم: یہ پہلی سعودی ریاست کے دور کا محل ہے»; gender: rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-riyaasat — entry page «رِیاسَت — اسم، مؤنث — حکومت، راج، بادشاہت» (all read at stage 4, 2026-10-12)
پہلی سعودی ریاست.note: The translated name both sources carry, in the words of the reference and of the reader's paper; the reference title «امارت درعیہ» is recorded for search and is not written. 'The Saudi state' (baiah) is «سعودی ریاست» (123 pages) and 'the modern Saudi state' «جدید سعودی ریاست» (3 pages: «جدید سعودی ریاست کے بانی»), so one noun names the state on three pages. Feminine, read on the dictionary page; exercised by the ordinal («پہلی …») and by «بنو جبر کی ریاست» on jabri-mosque. b2 round 1: the blind reader counted three labels on three pages (first, modern, plain) and nothing saying how they relate: the sources'. b2 round 2: the second blind reader, as the first: no page says what «پہلی» is counted against, or how the first, the plain and the 'modern' state relate. The sources'. «بنو جبر کی ریاست» now stands twice on jabri-mosque (summary and body). b2 round 3: the third reader, as the first two: the three names of the state on three pages 'looked like three names for one thing and so like a contradiction'. The sources'.

المزروعیہ.source: built from the Arabic spelling (rulings P1, P17); no Urdu attestation: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «المزروعیہ» 0 pages (API, counted at stage 4, 2026-10-12); gender by the generic written with it (Rekhta entry page read by b1: «مَحَلَّہ — اسم، مذکر»)
المزروعیہ.note: Pending: nothing in Urdu to verify the form against. A district of Hofuf, written with the Urdu generic before it, as b1 writes «محلہ النعاثل» and the reference writes «ہفوف کے محلہ الکوت»: «محلہ المزروعیہ» (body, area). Masculine by «محلہ»; not exercised.

الکوت.source: ur.wikipedia.org — the district of Hofuf in exactly the text's form, generic included: «… ہفوف کے محلہ الکوت میں ایک علمی خاندان میں پیدا ہوئے» (article «عبد اللطیف بن عبد الرحمن ملا», pageid 2484151; exact phrase «محلہ الکوت» 1 page; found at stage 4). Written «محلہ الکوت» on baiah (summary, body, area) and on jabri-mosque (summary, body, area), and once bare, in the sentence that follows its naming: «الکوت پرانے ہفوف کا قدیم ترین محلہ ہے۔» — a sentence of its own since round 2 (item N33). قلعہ العقیر.note: Verified as a construction: two verified parts in the attested order; the article-less form of the reference is the search variant the adopted entry «العقیر» already records. The title mirrors title_en (generic translated) and is the transliteration too, as with «مسجد جواثا»: the Arabic generic is the Urdu word, so no bracket and no gloss, and item N14 does not touch this title. معاہدہ العقیر.note: Verified as a construction: the reference's own word for the instrument, with the place name in the round's one form (the reference writes it without the article: search variant). گچ.note: P16: the Urdu word, not the loan for gypsum. On bubakr-ribat (a building material) and qubba-mosque («گچ کی ایک تختی»). Pending for the gender, which the text does not exercise, and for the sense: the dictionary's word is lime plaster, the source's is gypsum. STAGE 4: gender settled — FEMININE (the ambiguity stage 1 met is two senses on one page); one key and one gender for both batches (SHARED-07). Sense: the dictionary's word is the plaster used on walls, which is what the source's «الجص» is on these pages (a building material on bubakr-ribat and umzurainiq, a plaque and ornament on qubba-mosque and umzurainiq); the mineral's loan name is not written (P16). Not exercised in the text of b3 («گچ کی ایک تختی» agrees with «تختی»). STAGE 7 (round 1): unchanged; read blind in the text without a remark on its form. STAGE 7 (round 2): unchanged, verified. Recorded for the next reader: the second reader stopped on the word on bubakr-ribat and was not sure of the material (his item 28, moderate; he met it again on qubba-mosque); the first reader passed it on both pages. The plainer word for the mineral is a loan and is barred by the owner's rule (P16). One reader of two: the entry is not overruled; charged under fit on bubakr-ribat.
